title: AdaBins: Depth Estimation using Adaptive Bins
creator: Shariq Farooq Bhat KAUST shariq.bhat@kaust.edu.sa, Ibraheem Alhashim KAUST ibraheem.alhashim@kaust.edu.sa, Peter Wonka KAUST pwonka@gmail.com
description: Abstract We address the problem of estimating a high quality dense depth map from a single RGB input image. We start out with a baseline encoder-decoder convolutional neural network architecture and pose the question of how the global processing of information can help improve overall depth estimation.

title: Markovian linearization of random walks on groups
creator: Charles Bordenave, Bastien Dubail
description: Abstract In operator algebra, the linearization trick is a technique that reduces the study of a non-commutative polynomial evaluated at elements of an algebra 𝒜 \mathcal{A} to the study of a polynomial of degree one, evaluated on the enlarged algebra 𝒜 ⊗ M r ​ ( ℂ ) \mathcal{A}\otimes M_{r}(\mathbb{C}) , for some integer r r .

title: A Backward SDE Method for Uncertainty Quantification in Deep Learning
creator: Richard Archibald, Feng Bao, Yanzhao Cao, He Zhang
description: Abstract We develop a probabilistic machine learning method, which formulates a class of stochastic neural networks by a stochastic optimal control problem. An efficient stochastic gradient descent algorithm is introduced under the stochastic maximum principle framework. Numerical experiments for applications of stochastic neural networks are carried out to validate the effectiveness of our methodology.

title: Geometric weight-shifting operators on Hilbert modular forms in characteristic p p
creator: Fred Diamond
description: Abstract . We carry out a thorough study of weight-shifting operators on Hilbert modular forms in characteristic p p , generalizing the author’s prior work with Sasaki to the case where p p is ramified in the totally real field.

title: Demography of galactic technosignatures 2020 Demography of galactic technosignatures – A.0.4
creator: Claudio Grimaldi
description: Abstract Probabilistic arguments about the existence of technological life beyond Earth traditionally refer to the Drake equation to draw possible estimates of the number of technologically advanced civilizations releasing, either intentionally or not, electromagnetic emissions in the Milky Way. Here, we introduce other indicators than Drake’s number N D N_{D} to develop a demography of artificial emissions populating the Galaxy.

title: Rules of the Road: Safety and Liveness Guarantees for Autonomous Vehicles
creator: Karena X. Cai, Tung Phan-Minh, Soon-Jo Chung, Richard M. Murray
description: Abstract The ability to guarantee safety and progress for all vehicles is vital to the success of the autonomous vehicle industry. We present a framework for designing autonomous vehicle behavior in a way that is safe and guarantees progress for all agents. In this paper, we first introduce a new game paradigm which we term the quasi-simultaneous game.

title: Random quantum graphs
creator: Alexandru Chirvasitu, Mateusz Wasilewski
description: Abstract We prove a number of results to the effect that generic quantum graphs (defined via operator systems as in the work of Duan-Severini-Winter / Weaver) have few symmetries: for a Zariski-dense open set of tuples ( X 1 , ⋯ , X d ) (X_{1},\cdots,X_{d}) of traceless self-adjoint operators in the n × n n\times n matrix algebra the

title: Defect State Density and Orbital Localization in a-Si:H/c-Si Heterojunction and the Role of H
creator: Reza Vatan Meidanshahi, Stephen M. Goodnick, Dragica Vasileska
description: Abstract In this paper, we explore the effect of H and its bonding configurations on the defect state density and orbital localization of hydrogenated amorphous Si (a-Si:H)/crystalline Si (c-Si) heterostructures using density functional theory (DFT) studies of model interfaces between amorphous silicon (a-Si)/a-Si:H and c-Si.

title: Conjecture 𝒪 \mathcal{O} holds for some Horospherical Varieties of Picard Rank 1
creator: Lela Bones, Garrett Fowler, Lisa Schneider and Ryan M. Shifler
description: Abstract . Property 𝒪 \mathcal{O} for an arbitrary complex, Fano manifold X X , is a statement about the eigenvalues of the linear operator obtained from the quantum multiplication of the anticanonical class of X X . Conjecture 𝒪 \mathcal{O} is a conjecture that Property 𝒪 \mathcal{O} holds for any Fano variety.

title: Adamastor: a New Low Latency and Scalable Decentralized Anonymous Payment System
creator: Rui Morais, Paul Andrew Crocker, Simão Melo de Sousa
description: Abstract This paper presents Adamastor, a new low latency and scalable decentralized anonymous payment system, which is an extension of Ring Confidential Transactions (RingCT) that is compatible with consensus algorithms that use Delegated Proof of Stake (DPoS) as a defense mechanism against Sybil attacks.

title: Sharp Convergence Rates for Darcy’s Law
creator: Zhongwei Shen
description: Abstract This paper is concerned with Darcy’s law for an incompressible viscous fluid flowing in a porous medium. We establish the sharp O ⁡ ( ε ) O(\sqrt{\varepsilon}) convergence rate in a periodically perforated and bounded domain in ℝ d \mathbb{R}^{d} for d ≥ 2 d\geq 2 , where ε \varepsilon represents the size of solid obstacles.

title: Verifying liquidity of recursive Bitcoin contracts
creator: Massimo Bartoletti \rsuper a, Stefano Lande \rsuper a, Maurizio Murgia \rsuper b, Roberto Zunino \rsuper b
description: Abstract . Smart contracts — computer protocols that regulate the exchange of crypto-assets in trustless environments — have become popular with the spread of blockchain technologies. A landmark security property of smart contracts is liquidity : in a non-liquid contract, it may happen that some assets remain frozen, i.e. not redeemable by anyone.

title: Transverse single-spin asymmetries of midrapidity π 0 \pi^{0} and η \eta mesons in polarized p p + + p p collisions at s = 200 \sqrt{s}=200 GeV
creator: U.A. Acharya, C. Aidala, Y. Akiba, M. Alfred, V. Andrieux, N. Apadula, H. Asano, B. Azmoun, V. Babintsev, N.S. Bandara, K.N. Barish, S. Bathe, A. Bazilevsky, M. Beaumier, R. Belmont, A. Berdnikov, Y. Berdnikov, L. Bichon, B. Blankenship, D.S. Blau, J.S. Bok, V. Borisov, M.L. Brooks, J. Bryslawskyj,
description: Abstract We present a measurement of the transverse single-spin asymmetry for π 0 \pi^{0} and η \eta mesons in p ↑ p^{\uparrow} + + p p collisions in the pseudorapidity range | η | < 0.35 |\eta|<0.35 and at a center-of-mass energy of 200 GeV with the PHENIX detector at the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider.

title: Thermodynamic Consistent Neural Networks for Learning Material Interfacial Mechanics
creator: Jiaxin Zhang, Congjie Wei, Chenglin Wu
description: Abstract For multilayer materials in thin substrate systems, interfacial failure is one of the most challenges. The traction-separation relations (TSR) quantitatively describe the mechanical behavior of a material interface undergoing openings, which is critical to understand and predict interfacial failures under complex loadings.

title: One Explicitly Solvable Model For The Galton-Watson Processes In the Random Environment
description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by . In this paper, we study the Galton-Watson process in the random environment for the particular case when the number of the offsprings in each generation has the fractional linear generation function with random parameters. In this case, the distribution of N t N_{t} , the number of particles at the moment time t = 0 , 1 , 2 , ⋯ t=0,1,2,\cdots can be calculated explicitly.

title: Scalable Deep-Learning-Accelerated Topology Optimization for Additively Manufactured Materials
creator: Sirui Bi, Jiaxin Zhang, Guannan Zhang
description: Abstract Topology optimization (TO) is a popular and powerful computational approach for designing novel structures, materials, and devices. Two computational challenges have limited the applicability of TO to a variety of industrial applications. First, a TO problem often involves a large number of design variables to guarantee sufficient expressive power.

title: Finite-volume energy shift of the three-pion ground state
creator: Fabian Müller, Akaki Rusetsky, Tiansu Yu
description: Abstract Using the framework of nonrelativistic effective field theory, the finite-volume ground-state energy shift is calculated up to and including O ⁡ ( L − 6 ) O(L^{-6}) for the system of three pions in the channel with the total isospin I = 1 I=1 .

title: Reciprocal maximum likelihood degrees of diagonal linear concentration models
creator: Christopher Eur, Tara Fife, José Alejandro Samper, Tim Seynnaeve
description: Abstract We show that the reciprocal maximal likelihood degree (rmld) of a diagonal linear concentration model ℒ ⊆ ℂ n \mathcal{L}\subseteq\mathbb{C}^{n} of dimension r r is equal to ( − 2 ) r ​ χ M ​ ( 1 2 ) , (-2)^{r}\chi_{M}(\textstyle\frac{1}{2}), where χ M \chi_{M} is the characteristic polynomial of the matroid M M associated to ℒ \mathcal{L}

title: Approximation and localized polynomial frame on conic domains Thanks: The author is partially supported by Simons Foundation Grant #849676.
creator: Yuan Xu
description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Yuan Xu. Highly localized kernels constructed by orthogonal polynomials have been fundamental in the recent development of approximation and computational analysis on the unit sphere, unit ball, and several other regular domains. In this work, we first study homogeneous spaces that are assumed to contain highly localized kernels and establish a framework for approximation and localized tight frames in such spaces, which extends recent works on bounded regular domains.

title: Using Multiple Subwords to Improve English-Esperanto Automated Literary Translation Quality
creator: Alberto Poncelas, Jan Buts, James Hadley, Andy Way
description: Abstract Building Machine Translation (MT) systems for low-resource languages remains challenging. For many language pairs, parallel data are not widely available, and in such cases MT models do not achieve results comparable to those seen with high-resource languages. When data are scarce, it is of paramount importance to make optimal use of the limited material available.

title: Transverse momentum dependent forward neutron single spin asymmetries in transversely polarized p p + + p p collisions at s = 200 \sqrt{s}=200 GeV
creator: U.A. Acharya, C. Aidala, Y. Akiba, M. Alfred, V. Andrieux, N. Apadula, H. Asano, B. Azmoun, V. Babintsev, N.S. Bandara, K.N. Barish, S. Bathe, A. Bazilevsky, M. Beaumier, R. Belmont, A. Berdnikov, Y. Berdnikov, L. Bichon, B. Blankenship, D.S. Blau, J.S. Bok, V. Borisov, M.L. Brooks, J. Bryslawskyj,
description: Abstract In 2015, the PHENIX collaboration has measured very forward ( η > 6.8 \eta>6.8 ) single spin asymmetries of inclusive neutrons in transversely polarized proton-proton and proton-nucleus collisions at a center of mass energy of 200 GeV. A previous publication from this data set concentrated on the nuclear dependence of such asymmetries.

title: Contact Tracing Enhances the Efficiency of COVID-19 Group Testing
creator: Ritesh Goenka, Shu-Jie Cao, Chau-Wai Wong, Ajit Rajwade, Dror Baron
description: Abstract Group testing can save testing resources in the context of the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic. In group testing, we are given n n samples, one per individual, and arrange them into m < n m<n pooled samples, where each pool is obtained by mixing a subset of the n n individual samples.

title: Cohomology jump loci and absolute sets for singular varieties
creator: Leonardo A. Lerer
description: Abstract . We extend the notion of absolute subsets of Betti moduli spaces of smooth algebraic varieties to the case of normal varieties. As a consequence we prove that twisted cohomology jump loci in rank one over a normal variety are a finite union of translated subtori.

title: Privacy-Preserving Federated Learning for UAV-Enabled Networks: Learning-Based Joint Scheduling and Resource Management
creator: Helin Yang, Jun Zhao, Zehui Xiong, Kwok-Yan Lam, Sumei Sun, Liang Xiao
description: Abstract Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are capable of serving as flying base stations (BSs) for supporting data collection, artificial intelligence (AI) model training, and wireless communications. However, due to the privacy concerns of devices and limited computation or communication resource of UAVs, it is impractical to send raw data of devices to UAV servers for model training.

title: Insulated primes
creator: Abhimanyu Kumar, Anuraag Saxena
description: Abstract . The degree of insulation of a prime p p is defined as the largest interval around it in which no other prime exists. Based on this, the n n -th prime p n p_{n} is said to be insulated if and only if its degree of insulation is higher than its neighboring primes.

title: On linear shifts of finite type and their endomorphisms
creator: Tullio Ceccherini-Silberstein, Michel Coornaert, Xuan Kien Phung
description: Abstract . Let G G be a group and let A A be a finite-dimensional vector space over an arbitrary field K K . We study finiteness properties of linear subshifts Σ ⊂ A G \Sigma\subset A^{G} and the dynamical behavior of linear cellular automata τ : Σ → Σ \tau\colon\Sigma\to\Sigma .

title: Application of the Kovacic algorithm for the investigation of motion of a heavy rigid body with a fixed point in the Hess case.
description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by . Аннотация In 1890 German mathematician and physicist W. Hess [ 4 ] found new special case of integrability of Euler – Poisson equations of motion of a heavy rigid body with a fixed point. Nekrasov [ 17 , 18 ] proved that the solution of the problem of motion of a heavy rigid body with a fixed point under Hess conditions reduces to integrating the second order linear differential equation.

title: Soft x-ray detection for small satellites with a commercial CMOS sensor at room temperature
creator: Steve Tammes, Tyler Roth, Philip Kaaret, Casey DeRoo, Abdallah Elmaleh, Jessica L. McChesney, Fanny Rodolakis
description: Abstract Recently CMOS (complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor) sensors have progressed to a point where they may offer improved performance in imaging x-ray detection compared to the CCDs often used in x-ray satellites. We demonstrate x-ray detection in the soft x-ray band (250-1700 eV) by a commercially available back-illuminated Sony IMX290LLR CMOS sensor using the Advanced Photon Source at the Argonne National Laboratory.

title: HexGen and Hex2Spline: Polycube-based Hexahedral Mesh Generation and Spline Modeling for Isogeometric Analysis Applications in LS-DYNA
creator: Yuxuan Yu, Xiaodong Wei, Angran Li, Jialei Ginny Liu, Jeffrey He and Yongjie Jessica Zhang
description: Abstract In this paper, we present two software packages, HexGen and Hex2Spline, that seamlessly integrate geometry design with isogeometric analysis (IGA) in LS-DYNA. Given a boundary representation of a solid model, HexGen creates a hexahedral mesh by utilizing a semi-automatic polycube-based mesh generation method.

title: Two Families of Hypercyclic Non-Convolution Operators
creator: Alex Myers, Muhammadyusuf Odinaev, David Walmsley
description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Alex Myers, Muhammadyusuf Odinaev, David Walmsley. Let H ⁡ ( ℂ ) H(\mathbb{C}) be the set of all entire functions endowed with the topology of uniform convergence on compact sets. Let λ , b ∈ ℂ \lambda,b\in\mathbb{C} , let C λ , b : H ⁡ ( ℂ ) → H ⁡ ( ℂ ) C_{\lambda,b}:H(\mathbb{C})\to H(\mathbb{C}) be the composition operator C λ , b ​ f ​ ( z ) = f ⁡ ( λ ​ z + b ) C_{\lambda,b}f(z)=f(\lambda z+b) ,

title: Cyberbiosecurity: DNA Injection Attack in Synthetic Biology
creator: Dor Farbiash, Rami Puzis
description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Dor Farbiash, Rami Puzis. Today arbitrary synthetic DNA can be ordered online and delivered within several days. In order to regulate both intentional and unintentional generation of dangerous substances, most synthetic gene providers screen DNA orders. A weakness in the Screening Framework Guidance for Providers of Synthetic Double-Stranded DNA allows screening protocols based on this guidance to be circumvented using a generic obfuscation procedure inspired by early malware obfuscation techniques.

title: Two-coil Wireless Power Transfer System Configured in Series–Series Topology: Fundamental Dynamics and Limitations on Transmitted Power
creator: Binh Duc Truong, Thuy Thi-Thien Le, and Berardi Sensale-Rodriguez
description: Abstract The dynamics and performance of a two-coil resonant coupled wireless power transfer system (WPTS) are investigated. At high coupling coefficient between the two resonators, the frequency splitting phenomenon occurs, in which the power transferred to the load attains its maximum at two frequencies that are away from the resonance frequency.

title: A ∂ ¯ \bar{\partial} -steepest descent method for oscillatory Riemann-Hilbert problems
creator: Fudong Wang, Wen-Xiu Ma
description: Abstract We study the long-time asymptotic behavior of oscillatory Riemann-Hilbert problems (RHPs) arising in the mKdV hierarchy (reducing from the AKNS hierarchy). Our analysis is based on the idea of ∂ ¯ \bar{\partial} -steepest descent. We consider RHPs generated from the inverse scattering transform of the AKNS hierarchy with weighted Sobolev initial data.

title: The Brown measure of unbounded variables with free semicircular imaginary part
creator: Ching-Wei Ho
description: Abstract . Let x 0 x_{0} be an unbounded self-adjoint operator such that the Brown measure of x 0 x_{0} exists in the sense of Haagerup and Schultz. Also let σ ~ α \tilde{\sigma}_{\alpha} and σ β \sigma_{\beta} be semicircular variables with variances α ≥ 0 \alpha\geq 0 and β > 0 \beta>0 respectively.

title: Group superschemes
creator: A.Masuoka, A. N. Zubkov
description: Abstract . We develop a general theory of algebraic group superschemes, which are not necessarily affine. Our key result is a category equivalence between those group superschemes and Harish-Chandra pairs, which generalizes the result known for affine algebraic group superschemes.

title: PCPs: Patient Cardiac Prototypes
creator: Dani Kiyasseh, Tingting Zhu, David A. Clifton
description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Dani Kiyasseh, Tingting Zhu, David A. Clifton. Many clinical deep learning algorithms are population-based and difficult to interpret. Such properties limit their clinical utility as population-based findings may not generalize to individual patients and physicians are reluctant to incorporate opaque models into their clinical workflow. To overcome these obstacles, we propose to learn patient-specific embeddings, entitled patient cardiac prototypes (PCPs), that efficiently summarize the cardiac state of the patient.

title: On vanishing near corners of conductive transmission eigenfunctions
creator: Youjun Deng, Chaohua Duan, Hongyu Liu
description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Youjun Deng, Chaohua Duan, Hongyu Liu. In this paper, we consider the transmission eigenvalue problem associated with a general conductive transmission condition and study the geometric structures of the transmission eigenfunctions. We prove that under a mild regularity condition in terms of the Herglotz approximations of one of the pair of the transmission eigenfunctions, the eigenfunctions must be vanishing around a corner on the boundary.

title: Simultaneous recovery of surface heat flux and thickness of a solid structure by ultrasonic measurements
creator: Youjun Deng, Hongyu Liu, Xianchao Wang, Dong Wei, Liyan Zhu
description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Youjun Deng, Hongyu Liu, Xianchao Wang, Dong Wei, Liyan Zhu. This paper is concerned with a practical inverse problem of simultaneously reconstructing the surface heat flux and the thickness of a solid structure from the associated ultrasonic measurements. In a thermoacoustic coupling model, the thermal boundary condition and the thickness of a solid structure are both unknown, while the measurements of the propagation time by ultrasonic sensors are given.

title: CROCS: Clustering and Retrieval of Cardiac Signals Based on Patient Disease Class, Sex, and Age
creator: Dani Kiyasseh, Tingting Zhu, & David Clifton
description: Abstract The process of manually searching for relevant instances in, and extracting information from, clinical databases underpin a multitude of clinical tasks. Such tasks include disease diagnosis, clinical trial recruitment, and continuing medical education. This manual search-and-extract process, however, has been hampered by the growth of large-scale clinical databases and the increased prevalence of unlabelled instances.

title: Phase transitions in four-dimensional AdS black holes with a nonlinear electrodynamics source
creator: Ramón Bécar, P. A. González, Joel Saavedra, Yerko Vásquez, Bin Wang
description: Abstract In this work we consider black hole solutions to Einstein theory coupled to a nonlinear power-law electromagnetic field with a fixed exponent value. We study the extended phase space thermodynamics in canonical and grand canonical ensembles where the varying cosmological constant plays the role of an effective thermodynamic pressure.

title: HEDRA: A Bio-Inspired Modular Tensegrity Soft Robot With Polyhedral Parallel Modules
creator: Vishal Ramadoss*, Keerthi Sagar*, Mohamed Sadiq Ikbal, Jesus Hiram Lugo Calles, Matteo Zoppi
description: Abstract There is a surge of research interest in the field of tensegrity robotics. Robots developed under this paradigm provide many advantages and have distinguishing features in terms of structural compliance, dexterity, safety, and weight reduction. This paper proposes a new robotic mechanism based on tensegrity (‘tension-integrity’) robots and reconfigurable modular robots.

title: A Smoluchowski-Kramers approximation for an infinite dimensional system with state-dependent damping
creator: Sandra Cerrai, Guangyu Xi
description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Sandra Cerrai, Guangyu Xi. We study the validity of a Smoluchowski-Kramers approximation for a class of wave equations in a bounded domain of ℝ n \mathbb{R}^{n} subject to a state-dependent damping and perturbed by a multiplicative noise. We prove that in the small mass limit the solution converges to the solution of a stochastic quasilinear parabolic equation where a noise-induced extra drift is created.

title: Monte Carlo Tree Search for a single target search game on a 2-D lattice
creator: Elana Kozak, Scott Hottovy
description: Abstract Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) is a branch of stochastic modeling that utilizes decision trees for optimization, mostly applied to artificial intelligence (AI) game players. This project imagines a ?game? in which an AI player searches for a stationary target within a 2-D lattice.

title: Convergence of Rain Process Models to Point Processes
creator: Scott Hottovy, Samuel N. Stechmann
description: Abstract A moisture process with dynamics that switch after hitting a threshold gives rise to a rainfall process. This rainfall process is characterized by its random holding times for dry and wet periods. On average, the holding times for the wet periods are much shorter than the dry.

title: Latent Template Induction with Gumbel-CRFs Thanks: Work done during an internship at Alibaba DAMO Academy, in collaboration with PKU and Cornell.
description: Abstract Learning to control the structure of sentences is a challenging problem in text generation. Existing work either relies on simple deterministic approaches or RL-based hard structures. We explore the use of structured variational autoencoders to infer latent templates for sentence generation using a soft, continuous relaxation in order to utilize reparameterization for training.

title: The Awakening Beast in the Seyfert 1 Galaxy KUG 1141 + + 371 I. 2020 The Awakening Beast in the Seyfert 1 Galaxy KUG 1141 + + 371 I. – C
creator: Jiachen Jiang, Huaqing Cheng, Luigi C. Gallo, Luis C. Ho, Douglas J. K. Buisson, Andrew C. Fabian, Fiona A. Harrison, Michael L. Parker, Christopher S. Reynolds, James F. Steiner, John A. Tomsick, Dominic J. Walton, Weimin Yuan
description: Abstract KUG 1141 + + 371 is a Seyfert 1 galaxy that shows a simultaneous flux increase in the optical and UV bands in the past decade. For instance, the latest Swift observation in 2019 shows that the UVW2 flux of the AGN in KUG 1141 + + 371 has increased by over one order of magnitude since 2009.

title: The 𝔽 p {\mathbb{F}}_{p} -Selberg integral
creator: Richárd Rimányi ⋄ and Alexander Varchenko ⋆
description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Richárd Rimányi ⋄ and Alexander Varchenko ⋆. We prove an 𝔽 p {\mathbb{F}}_{p} -Selberg integral formula, in which the 𝔽 p {\mathbb{F}}_{p} -Selberg integral is an element of the finite field 𝔽 p {\mathbb{F}}_{p} with odd prime number p p of elements. The formula is motivated by analogy between multidimensional hypergeometric solutions of the KZ equations and polynomial solutions of the same equations reduced modulo p p .

title: Pressure Dependent Electronic Structure in CeRh 6 Ge 4
creator: Chao Cao, Jian-Xin Zhu
description: Abstract Using the state-of-art dynamical mean-field theory combined with density functional theory method, we have performed systematic study on the temperature and pressure dependent electronic structure of ferromagnetic quantum critical material candidate CeRh 6 Ge 4 . At -3.9 GPa and -8.

title: Reinforcement Learning based Distributed Control of Dissipative Networked Systems
creator: K. C. Kosaraju, S. Sivaranjani, W. Suttle, V. Gupta, J. Liu
description: Abstract We consider the problem of designing distributed controllers to stabilize a class of networked systems, where each subsystem is dissipative and designs a reinforcement learning based local controller to maximize an individual cumulative reward function. We develop an approach that enforces dissipativity conditions on these local controllers at each subsystem to guarantee stability of the entire networked system.

title: Enriching Load Data Using Micro-PMUs and Smart Meters
creator: Fankun Bu, Kaveh Dehghanpour, Zhaoyu Wang
description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Fankun Bu, Kaveh Dehghanpour, Zhaoyu Wang. In modern distribution systems, load uncertainty can be fully captured by micro-PMUs, which can record high-resolution data; however, in practice, micro-PMUs are installed at limited locations in distribution networks due to budgetary constraints. In contrast, smart meters are widely deployed but can only measure relatively low-resolution energy consumption, which cannot sufficiently reflect the actual instantaneous load volatility within each sampling interval.

title: Intrinsic Contribution to Non-linear Thermoelectric Effect
creator: Pankaj Bhalla
description: Abstract Irradiation of the strong light on the material leads to numerous non-linear effects that are essential to understand the physics of excited states of the system and for optoelectronics. Here, we study the non-linear thermoelectric effect due to the electric and thermal fields applied on a non-centrosymmetric system.

title: Multi-task GANs for Semantic Segmentation and Depth Completion with Cycle Consistency Thanks: This work was supported by the National Key Research and Development Program of China under Grant 2018YFC0809302, the National Natural Science Foundation of China under Grant Nos. 61988101, 61751305, 616731
creator: Chongzhen Zhang, Yang Tang, Senior Member, IEEE,
description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Chongzhen Zhang, Yang Tang, Senior Member, IEEE,. Semantic segmentation and depth completion are two challenging tasks in scene understanding, and they are widely used in robotics and autonomous driving. Although several studies have been proposed to jointly train these two tasks using some small modifications, like changing the last layer, the result of one task is not utilized to improve the performance of the other one despite that there are some similarities between these two tasks.

title: Accelerating MCMC algorithms through Bayesian Deep Networks
creator: Héctor Javier Hortúa, Riccardo Volpi, Dimitri Marinelli, Luigi Malagò
description: Abstract Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) algorithms are commonly used for their versatility in sampling from complicated probability distributions. However, as the dimension of the distribution gets larger, the computational costsfor a satisfactory exploration of the sampling space become challenging. Adaptive MCMC methods employing a choice of proposal distribution can address this issue speeding up the convergence.

title: Nonsingular transformations that are ergodic with isometric coefficients and not weakly doubly ergodic
creator: Beatrix Haddock, James Leng, Cesar E. Silva
description: Abstract . We study two properties of nonsingular and infinite measure-preserving ergodic systems: weak double ergodicity, and ergodicity with isometric coefficients. We show that there exist infinite measure-preserving transformations that are ergodic with isometric coefficients but are not weakly doubly ergodic; hence these two notions are not equivalent for infinite measure.

title: Learning geometry-image representation for 3D point cloud generation
creator: Lei Wang, Yuchun Huang, Pengjie Tao, Yaolin Hou, Yuxuan Liu
description: Abstract We study the problem of generating point clouds of 3D objects. Instead of discretizing the object into 3D voxels with huge computational cost and resolution limitations, we propose a novel geometry image based generator (GIG) to convert the 3D point cloud generation problem to a 2D geometry image generation problem.

title: Erasure-Resilient Sublinear-Time Graph Algorithms
creator: Amit Levi, Ramesh Krishnan S. Pallavoor, Sofya Raskhodnikova, Nithin Varma
description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Amit Levi, Ramesh Krishnan S. Pallavoor, Sofya Raskhodnikova, Nithin Varma. We investigate sublinear-time algorithms that take partially erased graphs represented by adjacency lists as input. Our algorithms make degree and neighbor queries to the input graph and work with a specified fraction of adversarial erasures in adjacency entries. We focus on two computational tasks: testing if a graph is connected or ε \varepsilon -far from connected and estimating the average degree.

title: Inflating Topic Relevance with Ideology: A Case Study of Political Ideology Bias in Social Topic Detection Models
creator: Meiqi Guo, Rebecca Hwa, Yu-Ru Lin, Wen-Ting Chung
description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Meiqi Guo, Rebecca Hwa, Yu-Ru Lin, Wen-Ting Chung. We investigate the impact of political ideology biases in training data. Through a set of comparison studies, we examine the propagation of biases in several widely-used NLP models and its effect on the overall retrieval accuracy. Our work highlights the susceptibility of large, complex models to propagating the biases from human-selected input, which may lead to a deterioration of retrieval accuracy, and the importance of controlling for these biases.

title: A comparison of handcrafted, parameterized, and learnable features for speech separation
creator: Wenbo Zhu, Mou Wang, Xiao-Lei Zhang, Susanto Rahardja
description: Abstract The design of acoustic features is important for speech separation. It can be roughly categorized into three classes: handcrafted, parameterized, and learnable features. Among them, learnable features, which are trained with separation networks jointly in an end-to-end fashion, become a new trend of modern speech separation research, e.g.

title: A characterization of X X for which spaces C p ​ ( X ) C_{p}(X) are distinguished and its applications Thanks: The research for the first named author is supported by the GAČR project 20-22230L and RVO: 67985840. He thanks also the Center For Advanced Studies in Mathematics of Ben-Gurion University
creator: Jerzy Ka̧kol, Arkady Leiderman
description: Abstract . We prove that the locally convex space C p ​ ( X ) C_{p}(X) of continuous real-valued functions on a Tychonoff space X X equipped with the topology of pointwise convergence is distinguished if and only if X X is a Δ \Delta -space in the sense of [ 21 ] .

title: Prediction of hidden-charm pentaquarks with double strangeness
creator: Fu-Lai Wang 1,2, Rui Chen 3, Xiang Liu 1,2,4
description: Abstract Inspired by the recent evidence of P c ​ s ​ ( 4459 ) P_{cs}(4459) reported by LHCb, we continue to perform the investigation of hidden-charm molecular pentaquarks with double strangeness, which are composed of an S S -wave charmed baryon Ξ c ( ′ , ∗ ) \Xi_{c}^{(\prime,*)} and an S S -wave anti-charmed-strange meson D ¯ s

title: Analytical Design for Full-space Spatial Power Dividers Using Metagratings
creator: Hamid Rajabalipanah, Ali Abdolali
description: Abstract We present a rigorous theoretical framework for designing full-space spatial power dividers using metagratings. In our study, the current restrictions of spatial power dividing platforms such as reflection-only performance, operating at normal incidence, and small reflection/refraction angles have been totally relaxed.

title: Implications of single field inflation in general cosmological scenarios on the nature of dark energy given the swampland conjectures
creator: Oem Trivedi
description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Oem Trivedi. Swampland Conjectures have attracted quite some interest in the Cosmological Community. They have been shown to have wide ranging implications , like Constraints on Inflationary Models, Primordial Black Holes etc. A particularly revealing insight on dark energy also shows that one can have the dark energy equation of state for a quintessence scenario to be signficantly different than -1 after one takes into account the refined dS conjecture.

title: Heterotic Complex Structure Moduli Stabilization for Elliptically Fibered Calabi-Yau Manifolds
creator: Wei Cui, Mohsen Karkheiran
description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Wei Cui, Mohsen Karkheiran. Complex structure moduli of a Calabi-Yau threefold in N = 1 N=1 supersymmetric heterotic compactifications can be stabilized by holomorphic vector bundles. The stabilized moduli are determined by a computation of Atiyah class. In this paper, we study how this mechanism work in the context of elliptically fibered Calabi-Yau manifolds where complex structure moduli space contains two kinds of moduli, ones from base and ones from fibration.

title: A Framework for Health-informed RUL-constrained Optimal Power Flow with Li-ion Batteries
creator: Jiahang Xie, Yu Weng, Hung D. Nguyen
description: Abstract Battery energy storage systems are widely adopted in grid-connected applications to mitigate the impact of intermittent renewable generations and enhance power system resiliency. Degradation of the battery during its service time is one of the major concerns in the deployment that strongly affects the long-term lifetime.

title: FROCC: Fast Random projection-based One-Class Classification
creator: Arindam Bhattacharya, Sumanth Varambally, Amitabha Bagchi, Srikanta Bedathur
description: Abstract We present Fast Random projection-based One-Class Classification (FROCC), an extremely efficient method for one-class classification. Our method is based on a simple idea of transforming the training data by projecting it onto a set of random unit vectors that are chosen uniformly and independently from the unit sphere, and bounding the regions based on separation of the data.

title: D ¯ s ( ∗ ) ​ D ( ∗ ) \bar{D}^{(*)}_{s}D^{(*)} molecular state with J P = 1 + J^{P}=1^{+}
creator: Yong-Jiang Xu 1 , Yong-Lu Liu 1 , Chun-Yu Cui 2 , and Ming-Qiu Huang 1,3
description: Abstract In this paper, we construct D ¯ s ( ∗ ) ​ D ( ∗ ) \bar{D}^{(*)}_{s}D^{(*)} -molecule-type interpolating currents J ( ± ) ​ μ ​ ( x ) J_{(\pm)\mu}(x) with J P = 1 + J^{P}=1^{+} , calculate the corresponding mass and magnetic moment using the QCD sum rule method and its extension in the weak electromagnetic

title: A Probabilistic Higher-order Fixpoint Logic
creator: Yo Mitani, Naoki Kobayashi, Takeshi Tsukada
description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Yo Mitani, Naoki Kobayashi, Takeshi Tsukada. We introduce PHFL, a probabilistic extension of higher-order fixpoint logic, which can also be regarded as a higher-order extension of probabilistic temporal logics such as PCTL and the μ p \mu^{p} -calculus. We show that PHFL is strictly more expressive than the μ p \mu^{p} -calculus, and that the PHFL model-checking problem for finite Markov chains is undecidable even for the μ \mu -only, order- 1 1 fragment of PHFL.

title: Dank or Not? – Analyzing and Predicting the Popularity of Memes on Reddit
creator: KBKate Barnes, TRTiernon Riesenmy, MDTMinh Duc Trinh, ELEli Lleshi, NBNóra Balogh, RMRoland Molontay
description: Abstract Internet memes have become an increasingly pervasive form of contemporary social communication that attracted a lot of research interest recently. In this paper, we analyze the data of 129,326 memes collected from Reddit in the middle of March, 2020, when the most serious coronavirus restrictions were being introduced around the world.

title: Charged-particle multiplicity dependence of charm-baryon-to-meson ratio in high-energy proton-proton collisions
creator: Yu Chen, Min He
description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Yu Chen, Min He. We propose that the charged-particle multiplicity dependence of the charm-baryon-to-meson ratio observed in high-energy p ​ p pp collisions can be explained by canonical treatment of quantum charges in the statistical hadronization model (SHM). Taking the full particle listings of PDG complemented by additional charm-baryon states from relativistic quark model predictions, we evaluate the canonical partition function and the charm-hadron chemical factors that measure the canonical suppression arising from the requirement of strict conservation of quantum charges.

title: Malaria Detection and Classificaiton
creator: Ruskin Raj Manku, Ayush Sharma, Anand Panchbhai
description: Abstract Malaria is a disease of global concern according to the World Health Organization. Billions of people in the world are at risk of Malaria today. Microscopy is considered the gold standard for Malaria diagnosis. Microscopic assessment of blood samples requires the need of trained professionals who at times are not available in rural areas where Malaria is a problem.

title: Morita equivalence of pseudogroups Thanks: The authors would like to thank the anonymous referee for their sterling work in reading the first draft of this paper. The second author’s research was funded by FCT/Portugal through project UIDB/04459/2020.
creator: M. V. Lawson, P. Resende
description: Abstract . We take advantage of the correspondence between pseudogroups and inverse quantal frames, and of the recent description of Morita equivalence for inverse quantal frames in terms of biprincipal bisheaves, to define Morita equivalence for pseudogroups and to investigate its applications. In particular, two pseudogroups are Morita equivalent if and only if their corresponding localic étale groupoids are.

title: Extreme Parametric Sensitivity in the Steady-State Photoisomerization of Two-Dimensional Model Rhodopsin
creator: Chern Chuang, Paul Brumer
description: Abstract We computationally studied the photoisomerization reaction of the retinal chromophore in rhodopsin using a two-state two-mode model coupled to thermal baths. Reaction quantum yields at the steady state (10 ps and beyond) were found to be considerably different than their transient values, suggesting a weak correlation between transient and steady-state dynamics in these systems.

title: ProtoPShare: Prototype Sharing for Interpretable Image Classification and Similarity Discovery
creator: Dawid Rymarczyk 1,2, Łukasz Struski 1, Jacek Tabor 1, Bartosz Zieliński 1,2, 1 Faculty of Mathematics and Computer Science, Jagiellonian University 6 6 Łojasiewicza Street, 30-348 Kraków, Poland, 2 Ardigen SA 76 76 Podole Street, 30-394 Kraków, Poland
description: Abstract In this paper, we introduce ProtoPShare, a self-explained method that incorporates the paradigm of prototypical parts to explain its predictions. The main novelty of the ProtoPShare is its ability to efficiently share prototypical parts between the classes thanks to our data-dependent merge-pruning.

title: Bjorken variable and scale dependence of quark transport coefficient in semi-inclusive lepton-production of hadron off nuclei
creator: Tian-Xing Bai, Chun-Gui Duan
description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Tian-Xing Bai, Chun-Gui Duan. Nuclear modification of hadron production in deep inelastic lepton-nucleus scattering can be applied to study the parton propagation mechanism in cold nuclear matter. By means of the analytic parameterization of quenching weight based on BDMPS formalism with the target nuclear geometry effect, the leading-order computations for hadron multiplicity ratios are performed with comparison to the HERMES charged pions production data on the quarks hadronization occurring outside the nucleus.

title: PRIMORDIAL BLACK HOLES AND MODIFICATION OF ZELDOVICH-NOVIKOV MECHANISM Paper presented at the Fourth Zeldovich meeting, an international conference in honor of Ya. B. Zeldovich held in Minsk, Belarus on September 7–11, 2020. Published by the recommendation of the special editors: S. Ya. Kilin, R. Ru
creator: © 2021. A. D. Dolgov, K. A. Postnov
description: Abstract Received: ; Revised: ; Accepted: . A review of the recent astronomical observations is presented and it is argued that the data strongly indicate that practically all observed black holes are primordial. A modified mechanism of the primordial black hole formation is described.

title: Optimizing Virtual Payment Channel Establishment in the Face of On-Path Adversaries PubID: pubid: This is the extended technical report of the work accepted at IFIP Networking 2024.
creator: Lukas Aumayr, Esra Ceylan, Yannik Kopyciok, Matteo Maffei, Pedro Moreno-Sanchez, Iosif Salem, Stefan Schmid
description: Abstract Payment channel networks (PCNs) are among the most promising solutions to the scalability issues in permissionless blockchains, by allowing parties to pay each other off-chain through a path of payment channels (PCs). However, routing transactions comes at a cost which is proportional to the number of intermediaries, since each charges a fee for the routing service.

title: Time-Resolved XUV absorption spectroscopy and magnetic circular dichroism at the Ni M 2 , 3 M_{2,3} -edges
creator: Marcel Hennes *, Benedikt Rösner, Valentin Chardonnet, Gheorghe S. Chiuzbaian, Renaud Delaunay, Florian Döring, Vitaliy A. Guzenko, Michel Hehn, Romain Jarrier, Armin Kleibert, Maxime Lebugle, Jan Lüning, Gregory Malinowski, Aladine Merhe, Denys Naumenko, Ivaylo P. Nikolov, Ignacio Lopez-Quintas, Em
description: Abstract Ultrashort optical pulses can trigger a variety of non-equilibrium processes in magnetic thin films affecting electrons and spins on femtosecond timescales. In order to probe the charge and magnetic degrees of freedom simultaneously, we developed an x-ray streaking technique that has the advantage of providing a jitter-free picture of absorption cross section changes.

title: Quantum quench in a driven Ising chain
creator: Neil J. Robinson, Isaac Pérez Castillo, Edgar Guzmán-González
description: Abstract We consider the Ising chain driven by oscillatory transverse magnetic fields. For certain parameter regimes, we reveal a hidden integrable structure in the problem, which allows access to the exact time-evolution in this driven quantum system. We compute time-evolved one- and two-point functions following a quench that activates the driving.

title: Google Searches and COVID-19 Cases in Saudi Arabia: A Correlation Study
creator: Btool Hamoui, Abdulaziz Alashaikh, Eisa Alanazi
description: Abstract Background : The outbreak of the new coronavirus disease (COVID-19) has affected human life to a great extent on a worldwide scale. During the coronavirus pandemic, public health professionals at the early outbreak faced an extraordinary challenge to track and quantify the spread of disease.

title: There and Back Again: Learning to Simulate Radar Data for Real-World Applications
creator: Rob Weston, Oiwi Parker Jones, Ingmar Posner
description: Abstract Simulating realistic radar data has the potential to significantly accelerate the development of data-driven approaches to radar processing. However, it is fraught with difficulty due to the notoriously complex image formation process. Here we propose to learn a radar sensor model capable of synthesising faithful radar observations based on simulated elevation maps.

title: Presentations of algebras in chain complexes
creator: Brice Le Grignou
description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Brice Le Grignou. The goal of this article is to describe several presentations of the infinity category of algebras over some monad on the infinity category of chain complexes. Introduction Many categories encountered in Algebra are presentable. This means that for such a category \mathsf{C} , one can find a small category \mathsf{D} and an equivalence relating \mathsf{C} to the full subcategory of \mathrm{Fun}\left(\mathsf{D}^{\mathrm{op}},\mathsf{Set}\right) spanned by functors F:\mathsf{D}\to\mathsf{Set} that satisfy some locality conditions.

title: Mate-Nevai-Totik theorem for Krein systems Thanks: The work is supported by Ministry of Science and Higher Education of the Russian Federation, agreement № 075–15–2019–1619.
creator: Pavel Gubkin
description: Abstract . We prove the Cesàro boundedness of eigenfunctions of the Dirac operator on the half-line with a square-summable potential. The proof is based on the theory of Krein systems and, in particular, on the continuous version of a theorem by A. Mate, P. Nevai and V. Totik from 1991. 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification 34L40, 42C05 1. Introduction 1.1.

title: Rota-Baxter operators on cocommutative Hopf algebras
description: Abstract We generalize the notion of a Rota-Baxter operator on groups and the notion of a Rota-Baxter operator of weight 1 on Lie algebras and define and study the notion of a Rota-Baxter operator on a cocommutative Hopf algebra H H .

title: Reinforcement Learning in Linear Quadratic Deep Structured Teams: Global Convergence of Policy Gradient Methods
creator: Vida Fathi, Jalal Arabneydi, Amir G. Aghdam
description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Vida Fathi, Jalal Arabneydi, Amir G. Aghdam. In this paper, we study the global convergence of model-based and model-free policy gradient descent and natural policy gradient descent algorithms for linear quadratic deep structured teams. In such systems, agents are partitioned into a few sub-populations wherein the agents in each sub-population are coupled in the dynamics and cost function through a set of linear regressions of the states and actions of all agents.

title: GitHub-OSS Fixit: Fixing bugs at scale in a Software Engineering Course
creator: Shin Hwei Tan 1 , Chunfeng Hu 2 , Ziqiang Li 3 , Xiaowen Zhang 4 and Ying Zhou 5
description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Shin Hwei Tan 1 , Chunfeng Hu 2 , Ziqiang Li 3 , Xiaowen Zhang 4 and Ying Zhou 5. Many studies have shown the benefits of introducing open-source projects into teaching Software Engineering (SE) courses.

title: Reinforcement Learning in Nonzero-sum Linear Quadratic Deep Structured Games: Global Convergence of Policy Optimization
creator: Masoud Roudneshin, Jalal Arabneydi, Amir G. Aghdam
description: Abstract We study model-based and model-free policy optimization in a class of nonzero-sum stochastic dynamic games called linear quadratic (LQ) deep structured games. In such games, players interact with each other through a set of weighted averages (linear regressions) of the states and actions.

title: Paths in tournaments, a simple proof of Rosenfeld’s Conjecture
creator: Charbel Bou Hanna
description: Abstract Rosenfeld Conjectured [ 7 ] in 1972 that there exists an integer K ≥ 8 K\geq 8 such that any tournament of order n ≥ K n\geq K contains any Hamiltonian oriented path. In 2000, Havet and Thomassé [ 5 ] proved this conjecture for any tournament with exactly 3 exceptions. We give a simplified proof of this fact.

title: Confinement and moduli locking of Alice strings and monopoles
creator: Muneto Nitta
description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Muneto Nitta. We argue that strings (vortices) and monopoles are confined, when fields receiving nontrivial Aharonov-Bohm (AB) phases around a string develop vacuum expectation values (VEVs). We illustrate this in an S ​ U ​ ( 2 ) × U ⁡ ( 1 ) SU(2)\times U(1) gauge theory with charged triplet complex scalar fields admitting Alice strings and monopoles, by introducing charged doublet scalar fields receiving nontrivial AB phases around the Alice string.

title: Socioeconomic Impact of Emerging Mobility Markets and Implementation Strategies
creator: Ioannis Vasileios Chremos, Student Member, IEEE, Andreas A. Malikopoulos, Senior Member, IEEE
description: Abstract Emerging mobility systems such as connected and automated vehicles (CAVs) provide the most intriguing opportunity for more accessible, safe, and efficient transportation. CAVs are expected to significantly improve safety by eliminating the human factor and ensure transportation efficiency by allowing users to monitor transportation network conditions and make better operating decisions.

title: BPS deformations of the Skyrme model
creator: J. M. Queiruga
description: Abstract We study several deformations of the Skyrme model in three dimensions with self-dual sectors of arbitrary baryonic charge. We show that, for a family of background metrics as well as for a family of field dependent couplings, the model has one BPS sector, which may have any topological charge.

title: On Computationally Efficient Subsystems of Propositional Logic
creator: Inga Lev
description: Abstract In this paper, we show that the derivability problem for the primal propositional logic remains solvable in polynomial time upon adding a certain form of the principle of equivalent form substitution; and that, upon adding another form of this principle, it becomes co-NP-hard.

title: Residuation in twist products and pseudo-Kleene posets
creator: Ivan Chajda, Helmut Länger
description: Abstract M. Busaniche, R. Cignoli, C. Tsinakis and A. M. Wille showed that every residuated lattice induces a residuation on its full twist product. For their construction they used also lattice operations. We generalize this problem to left-residuated groupoids which need not be lattice-ordered. Hence, for the full twist product we cannot use the same construction.

title: Conserved Kardar-Parisi-Zhang equation: Role of quenched disorder in determining universality
creator: Sudip Mukherjee
description: Abstract We study the stochastically driven conserved Kardar-Parisi-Zhang (CKPZ) equation with quenched disorders. Short-ranged quenched disorders is found to be a relevant perturbation on the pure CKPZ equation at one dimension, and as a result, a new universality class different from pure CKPZ equation appears to emerge.

title: Scaling or multiscaling: Varieties of universality in a driven nonlinear model
creator: Sudip Mukherjee, Abhik Basu
description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Sudip Mukherjee, Abhik Basu. Physical understanding of how the interplay between symmetries and nonlinear effects can control the scaling and multiscaling properties in a coupled driven system, such as magnetohydrodynamic turbulence or turbulent binary fluid mixtures, remains elusive till the date. To address this generic issue, we construct a conceptual nonlinear hydrodynamic model, parametrised jointly by the nonlinear coefficients, and the spatial scaling of the variances of the advecting stochastic velocity and the stochastic additive driving force, respectively.

title: Fixing Left and Right: Assignment of Chiral Elemental Crystal Structures using Kikuchi Diffraction
creator: Aimo Winkelmann, Grzegorz Cios, Tomasz Tokarski \orcidT, Piotr Bała \orcidP, Yuri Grin, Ulrich Burkhardt
description: Abstract Crystals of the chemical elements manganese, tellurium, and selenium can show the effects of handedness. In order to sense the possible effects of a changing sense of chirality on the properties of samples from these elements, the potential presence of two, enantiomorphic, physically different, variants of these elemental crystal structures needs to be resolved in crystallographic analyses.

title: WIP: Short-Term Flow-Based Bandwidth Forecasting using Machine Learning
creator: Maxime Labonne, Jorge López, Claude Poletti, Jean-Baptiste Munier
description: Abstract This paper proposes a novel framework to predict traffic flows’ bandwidth ahead of time. Modern network management systems share a common issue: the network situation evolves between the moment the decision is made and the moment when actions (countermeasures) are applied. This framework converts packets from real-life traffic into flows containing relevant features.

title: Hawking radiation of a multi-fractional Schwarzschild black hole
creator: Peng Huang, Fang-Fang Yuan
description: Abstract Following the initial work of Calcagni et al. on the black holes in multi-fractional theories, we focus on the Schwarzschild black hole in multi-fractional theory with q q -derivatives. After presenting its Hawking and Hayward temperatures in detail, we verify these results by appealing to the well-known Hamilton-Jacobi and null geodesic methods of the tunnelling approach to Hawking radiation.

title: Scaling down Deep Learning
creator: Sam Greydanus
description: Abstract Though deep learning models have taken on commercial and political relevance, many aspects of their training and operation remain poorly understood. This has sparked interest in ‘‘science of deep learning’’ projects, many of which are run at scale and require enormous amounts of time, money, and electricity. But how much of this research really needs to occur at scale?

title: Translation-invariant interpolation of parametric dictionaries Thanks: The authors thank the project “ANR BECOSE” (ANR-15-CE23-0021) for its support.
creator: Frédéric Champagnat, Cédric Herzet
description: Abstract In this communication, we address the problem of approximating the atoms of a parametric dictionary 𝒜 = { 𝒂 ⁡ ( 𝜽 ) : 𝜽 ∈ Θ } \mathcal{A}=\{{\boldsymbol{a}}(\boldsymbol{\theta}):\boldsymbol{\theta}\in\Theta\} , commonly encountered in the context of sparse representations in “continuous” dictionaries.

title: Approximation algorithms for hitting subgraphs
creator: Noah Brüstle, Tal Elbaz, Hamed Hatami, Onur Kocer, Bingchan Ma
description: Abstract Let H H be a fixed undirected graph on k k vertices. The H H -hitting set problem asks for deleting a minimum number of vertices from a given graph G G in such a way that the resulting graph has no copies of H H as a subgraph.

title: Model sets with Euclidean internal space
creator: Mauricio Allendes Cerda, Daniel Coronel
description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Mauricio Allendes Cerda, Daniel Coronel. We give an almost dynamical characterization of inter-model sets with Euclidean internal space. This characterization is similar to previous results for general inter-model sets obtained independently by Baake, Lenz and Moody, and Aujogue.

title: Subharmonic Functions, Conformal Metrics, and CAT(0) Thanks: This research was initiated at the Bedlewo Mathematical Research and Conference Center where both authors were supported by the Polish Academy of Sciences. We thank them for their hospitality. GJM is supported in part by a grant from the N

description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by David A. Herron, Gaven J. Martin. We present an analytical proof that certain natural metric planar universal covers are Hadamard metric spaces. In particular if ρ = φ ∘ u \rho=\varphi\circ u where u u is locally Lipschitz and subharmonic in Ω \Omega , φ \varphi is positive and increasing on an interval containing u ⁡ ( Ω ) u(\Omega) with log ⁡ φ \log\varphi convex, and if the metric space ( Ω , ρ ⁡ ( z ) ​ | d ​ z

title: Radiative cooling induced by time-symmetry breaking in periodically-driven systems
creator: Riccardo Messina, Annika Ott, Christoph Kathmann, Svend-Age Biehs, Philippe Ben-Abdallah
description: Abstract We theoretically study the thermal relaxation of many-body systems under the action of oscillating external fields. When the magnitude or the orientation of a field is modulated around values where the pairwise heat-exchange conductances depend non-linearly on this field, we demonstrate that the time symmetry is broken during the evolution of temperatures over a modulation cycle.

title: Improved Semantic Role Labeling using Parameterized Neighborhood Memory Adaptation
creator: Ishan Jindal, Ranit Aharonov, Siddhartha Brahma, Huaiyu Zhu, Yunyao Li
description: Abstract Deep neural models achieve some of the best results for semantic role labeling. Inspired by instance-based learning that utilizes nearest neighbors to handle low-frequency context-specific training samples, we investigate the use of memory adaptation techniques in deep neural models.

title: On the Density arising from the Domain of Attraction of an Operator interpolating between Sum and Supremum: the α \alpha -Sun Operator
creator: N.S. Witte, P.E. Greenwood
description: Abstract We explore the analytic properties of the density function h ⁡ ( x , γ , α ) h(x;\gamma,\alpha) , x ∈ ( 0 , ∞ ) x\in(0,\infty) , γ > 0 \gamma>0 , 0 < α < 1 0<\alpha<1 which arises as a normed limit from the domain of attraction problem for an operator interpolating between the supremum

title: HARMONIC FORMS, MINIMAL SURFACES AND NORMS ON COHOMOLOGY OF HYPERBOLIC 3 3 -MANIFOLDS
creator: Xiaolong Hans Han
description: Abstract We bound the L 2 L^{2} -norm of an L 2 L^{2} harmonic 1 1 -form in an orientable cusped hyperbolic 3 3 -manifold M M by its topological complexity, measured by the Thurston norm, up to a constant depending on M M . This generalizes two inequalities of Brock and Dunfield.

title: An algorithm for the automatic deglitching of x-ray absorption spectroscopy data
creator: Samuel M, Marco A
description: Abstract Analysis of x-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) data often involves the removal of artifacts or glitches from the acquired signal, a process commonly known as deglitching . Glitches result either from specific orientations of monochromator crystals or from scattering by crystallites in the sample itself.

title: Superelliptic curves with large Galois images
creator: Pip Goodman
description: Abstract Let r > 2 r>2 and ℓ \ell be primes. In this paper we study the mod ℓ \ell Galois representations attached to curves of the form y r = f ⁡ ( x ) y^{r}=f(x) where f f is monic and has coefficients belonging to the r r th cyclotomic field.

title: Discrete gravity dynamics from effective spin foams
creator: Seth K. Asante, Bianca Dittrich, Hal M. Haggard
description: Abstract The first computation of a spin foam dynamics that provides a test of the quantum equations of motions of gravity is presented. Specifically, a triangulation that includes an inner edge is treated. The computation leverages the recently introduced effective spin foam models, which are particularly numerically efficient.

title: Optical focusing of Bose-Einstein condensates
creator: A. M. Kordbacheh, S. S. Szigeti, A. M. Martin
description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by A. M. Kordbacheh, S. S. Szigeti, A. M. Martin. We theoretically investigate the optical focusing of a rubidium Bose-Einstein condensate onto a planar surface. Our analysis uses a Gaussian variational method that includes the effects of two-body atom-atom interactions and three-body recombination losses. The essential factors such as the width, peak density and atom loss rate of the focused BEC profile on the surface are investigated and compared to Gross-Pitaevskii numerical simulations.

title: Sedimentation of a Colloidal Monolayer Down an Inclined Plane
creator: B. Sprinkle, S. Wilken, S. Karapetyan, M. Tanaka, Z. Chen, J. R. Cruise, B. Delmotte, M. M. Driscoll, P. Chaikin, and A. Donev
description: Abstract We study the driven collective dynamics of a colloidal monolayer sedimentating down an inclined plane. The action of the gravity force parallel to the bottom wall creates a flow around each colloid, and the hydrodynamic interactions among the colloids accelerate the sedimentation as the local density increases.

title: The Difference λ \lambda -calculus: A Language for Difference Categories
creator: Mario Alvarez-Picallo, C.-H. Luke Ong
description: Abstract . Cartesian difference categories are a recent generalisation of Cartesian differential categories which introduce a notion of “infinitesimal” arrows satisfying an analogue of the Kock-Lawvere axiom, with the axioms of a Cartesian differential category being satisfied only “up to an infinitesimal perturbation”.

title: Hybrid coupling optomechanically assisted nonreciprocal photon blockade
creator: Yong-Pan Gao, Chuan Wang
description: Abstract The properties of open quantum system in quantum information science is now extensively investigated more generally by the research community as a fundamental issue for a variety of applications. Usually, the states of the open quantum system might be disturbed by the decoherence which will reduce the fidelity in the quantum information processing.

title: Multi-scale Adaptive Task Attention Network for Few-Shot Learning
creator: Haoxing Chen, Huaxiong Li, Yaohui Li, Chunlin Chen Nanjing University { \{ haoxingchen, yaohuili } \} @smail.nju.edu.cn, { \{ huaxiongli, clchen } \} @nju.edu.cn
description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Haoxing Chen, Huaxiong Li, Yaohui Li, Chunlin Chen Nanjing University { \{ haoxingchen, yaohuili } \} @smail.nju.edu.cn, { \{ huaxiongli, clchen } \} @nju.edu.cn. The goal of few-shot learning is to classify unseen categories with few labeled samples. Recently, the low-level information metric-learning based methods have achieved satisfying performance, since local representations (LRs) are more consistent between seen and unseen classes.

title: Value Function Based Performance Optimization of Deep Learning Workloads
creator: Benoit Steiner, Chris Cummins, Horace He, Hugh Leather
description: Abstract As machine learning techniques become ubiquitous, the efficiency of neural network implementations is becoming correspondingly paramount. Frameworks, such as Halide and TVM, separate out the algorithmic representation of the network from the schedule that determines its implementation. Finding good schedules, however, remains extremely challenging.

title: A Near-Optimal Parallel Algorithm for Joining Binary Relations Thanks: The research of Bas Ketsman was partially supported by FWO-grant G062721N. The research of Dan Suciu was partially supported by projects NSF IIS 1907997 and NSF-BSF 2109922. The research of Yufei Tao was partially supported by GR
creator: Bas Ketsman, Dan Suciu, Yufei Tao
description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Bas Ketsman, Dan Suciu, Yufei Tao. We present a constant-round algorithm in the massively parallel computation (MPC) model for evaluating a natural join where every input relation has two attributes. Our algorithm achieves a load of O ~ ​ ( m / p 1 / ρ ) \tilde{O}(m/p^{1/\rho}) where m m is the total size of the input relations, p p is the number of machines, ρ \rho is the join’s fractional edge covering number, and O ~ ( .

title: Intergalactic medium dispersion measures of fast radio bursts estimated from IllustrisTNG simulation and their cosmological applications
creator: Z. J. Zhang, K. Yan, C. M. Li, G. Q. Zhang, F. Y. Wang
description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Z. J. Zhang, K. Yan, C. M. Li, G. Q. Zhang, F. Y. Wang. Fast radio bursts (FRBs) are millisecond-duration radio transients and can be used as a cosmological probe. However, the dispersion measure (DM) contributed by intergalactic medium (IGM) is hard to be distinguished from other components. In this paper, we use the IllustrisTNG simulation to realistically estimate the D ​ M IGM DM_{\rm IGM} up to z ∼ 9 z\sim 9 .

title: Modelling Verbal Morphology in Nen
creator: Saliha Muradoğlu Nicholas Evans Ekaterina Vylomova
description: Abstract Nen verbal morphology is remarkably complex; a transitive verb can take up to 1,740 1,740 unique forms. The combined effect of having a large combinatoric space and a low-resource setting amplifies the need for NLP tools. Nen morphology utilises distributed exponence – a non-trivial means of mapping form to meaning.

title: Blind signal decomposition of various word embeddings based on join and individual variance explained (JIVE)
creator: Yikai Wang, Weijian Li
description: Abstract In recent years, natural language processing (NLP) has become one of the most important areas with various applications in human’s life. As the most fundamental task, the field of word embedding still requires more attention and research. Currently, existing works about word embedding are focusing on proposing novel embedding algorithms and dimension reduction techniques on well-trained word embeddings.

title: Coherent transverse instability of bunched beams in circular accelerators
creator: V. Balbekov
description: Abstract CONTENT 1. Basic relations 1.1. Definitions and designations. 1.2. Equation of coherent betatron oscillations (smooth linear betatron oscillations; nonlinear space charge field; wake field; chromaticity; coherent oscillations; Laplace transform) . 1.3. Landau damping of a coasting beam (restricted or unrestricted momentum spread?) . 2. Single bunch general equations (short wake) . 3. Hollow bunch in a square well 3.1.

title: Counting Restricted Partitions of Integers into Fractions: Symmetry and Modes of the Generating Function and a Connection to ω ⁡ ( t ) \omega(t)
creator: Z. Hoelscher, E. Palsson
description: Abstract - Motivated by the study of integer partitions, we consider partitions of integers into fractions of a particular form, namely with constant denominators and distinct odd or even numerators. When numerators are odd, the numbers of partitions for integers smaller than the denominator form symmetric patterns.

title: End-to-End Video Instance Segmentation with Transformers
creator: Yuqing Wang 1, Zhaoliang Xu 1, Xinlong Wang 2, Chunhua Shen 2, Baoshan Cheng 1, Hao Shen 1, Huaxia Xia 1 1 Meituan 2 The University of Adelaide, Australia yuqingwang1029@gmail.com, shenhao04@meituan.com
description: Abstract Video instance segmentation (VIS) is the task that requires simultaneously classifying, segmenting and tracking object instances of interest in video. Recent methods typically develop sophisticated pipelines to tackle this task. Here, we propose a new video instance segmentation framework built upon Transformers, termed VisTR, which views the VIS task as a direct end-to-end parallel sequence decoding/prediction problem.

title: Training and Inference for Integer-Based Semantic Segmentation Network
creator: Jiayi Yang, Lei Deng, Yukuan Yang, Yuan Xie, Guoqi Li
description: Abstract Semantic segmentation has been a major topic in research and industry in recent years. However, due to the computation complexity of pixel-wise prediction and backpropagation algorithm, semantic segmentation has been demanding in computation resources, resulting in slow training and inference speed and large storage space to store models.

title: On the Grothendieck ring of the sequence of walled Brauer algebras
creator: Pei Wang, Yanbo Li †
description: Abstract . In this paper, we provide a diagrammatic approach to study the branching rules for cell modules on a sequence of walled Brauer algebras. This approach also allows us to calculate the structure constants of multiplication over the Grothendieck ring of the sequence. † † † Corresponding author: liyanbo707@163.com † † 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification: 16D90; 16G10; 16E20.

title: Variational Discrete Action Theory
creator: Zhengqian Cheng and Chris A. Marianetti
description: Abstract Here we propose the Variational Discrete Action Theory (VDAT) to study the ground state properties of quantum many-body Hamiltonians. VDAT is a variational theory based on the sequential product density matrix (SPD) ansatz, characterized by an integer 𝒩 \mathcal{N} , which monotonically approaches the exact solution with increasing 𝒩 \mathcal{N} .

title: Constraints on Maximal Entanglement Under Groups of Permutations
creator: Alexander Meill, Jayden Butts, and Elijah Sanderson
description: Abstract We provide a simplified characterization of entanglement in physical systems which are symmetric under the action of subgroups of the symmetric group acting on the party labels. Sets of entanglements are inherently equal, lying in the same orbit under the group action, which we demonstrate for cyclic, dihedral, and polyhedral groups.

title: Weil-Chatelet Groups of Rational Elliptic Surfaces
creator: Nadir Hajouji
description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Nadir Hajouji. We classify pairs ( S , γ ) (S,\gamma) , consisting of a rational elliptic surface S S and a Galois cover γ \gamma of the base, which satisfy a condition we call ℒ \mathcal{L} -stability. We explain how to use the theory of Mordell-Weil lattices to compute the kernel of the restriction maps of Weil-Chatelet groups for ℒ \mathcal{L} -stable pairs.

title: Pure Gauss sums and skew Hadamard difference sets Thanks: The author acknowledges the support by JSPS under Grant-in-Aid for Scientific Research (C) 20K03719.
creator: Koji Momihara
description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Koji Momihara. Chowla (1962), McEliece (1974), Evans (1977, 1981) and Aoki (1997, 2004, 2012) studied Gauss sums, some integral powers of which are in the field of rational numbers. Such Gauss sums are called pure . In particular, Aoki (2004) gave a necessary and sufficient condition for a Gauss sum to be pure in terms of Dirichlet characters modulo the order of the multiplicative character involved.

title: Signatures of the BCS-BEC crossover in the yrast spectra of Fermi quantum rings
creator: Ulrich Ebling, Ali Alavi, Joachim Brand
description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Ulrich Ebling, Ali Alavi, Joachim Brand. We study properties of the lowest energy states at non-zero total momentum (yrast states) of the Hubbard model for spin- 1 2 \frac{1}{2} fermions in the quantum ring configuration with attractive on-site interaction at low density. In the one-dimensional (1D) case we solve the Hubbard model using the Bethe ansatz, while for the crossover into the 2D regime we use the Full-Configuration-Interaction Quantum Monte-Carlo method (FCIQMC) to obtain the yrast states for the spin-balanced Fermi system.

title: Inter-layer Transition in Neural Architecture Search
creator: Benteng Ma 1,2, Jing Zhang 2, Yong Xia 1, Dacheng Tao 2, 1 Northwestern Polytechnical University, China 2 The University of Sydney, Australia
description: Abstract Differential Neural Architecture Search (NAS) methods represent the network architecture as a repetitive proxy directed acyclic graph (DAG) and optimize the network weights and architecture weights alternatively in a differential manner. However, existing methods model the architecture weights on each edge (i.e.

title: Foundations of the Variational Discrete Action Theory
creator: Zhengqian Cheng and Chris A. Marianetti
description: Abstract Variational wave functions and Green’s functions are two important paradigms for solving quantum Hamiltonians, each having their own advantages. Here we detail the Variational Discrete Action Theory (VDAT), which exploits the advantages of both paradigms in order to approximately solve the ground state of quantum Hamiltonians.

title: Predictive case control designs for modification learning
creator: W. Katherine Tan, Patrick J. Heagerty
description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by W. Katherine Tan, Patrick J. Heagerty. Prediction models for clinical outcomes, originally developed using a source dataset, may additionally be applied to a new cohort. Prior to accurate application, the source model needs to be updated through external validation procedures such as modification learning. Model modification learning involves the dual goals of recalibrating overall predictions as well as revising individual feature effects, and generally requires the collection of an adequate sample of true outcome labels from the new setting.

title: Ultra-fast model emulation with PRISM; analyzing the Meraxes galaxy formation model Journal: ApJS
creator: Ellert van der Velden, Alan R. Duffy, Darren Croton, Simon J. Mutch
description: Abstract We demonstrate the potential of an emulator-based approach to analyzing galaxy formation models in the domain where constraining data is limited. We have applied the open-source Python package Prism to the galaxy formation model Meraxes . Meraxes is a semi-analytic model, purposefully built to study the growth of galaxies during the Epoch of Reionization (EoR).

title: Algebraic correlations and anomalous fluctuations in ordered flocks of Janus particles fueled by an AC electric field
creator: Junichiro Iwasawa, Daiki Nishiguchi, Masaki Sano
description: Abstract We study the polar collective dynamics of Janus colloidal particles fueled by an AC electric field. When the density is high enough, the polar interactions between the particles induce a polar orientationally ordered state which exhibits features reminiscent of the Vicsek model such as true long-range order and giant number fluctuations.

title: Two-photon superbunching effect of broadband chaotic stationary light at femtosecond timescale based on cascaded Michelson interferometer
creator: Sheng Luo, Yu Zhou, Huaibin Zheng, Jianbin Liu, Hui Chen, Yuchen He, Wanting Xu, Shuanghao Zhang, Fuli Li, Zhuo Xu
description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Sheng Luo, Yu Zhou, Huaibin Zheng, Jianbin Liu, Hui Chen, Yuchen He, Wanting Xu, Shuanghao Zhang, Fuli Li, Zhuo Xu. It is challenging for observing superbunching effect with true chaotic light, here we propose and demonstrate a method to achieve superbunching effect of g ( 2 ) ​ ( 0 ) = 2.42 ± 0.02 g^{(2)}(0)=2.42\pm 0.02 with broadband stationary chaotic light based on a cascaded Michelson interferometer (CMI), exceeding the theoretical upper limit of 2 for the two-photon bunching effect of chaotic light.

title: A Customizable Dynamic Scenario Modeling and Data Generation Platform for Autonomous Driving
creator: Jay Shenoy, Edward Kim, Xiangyu Yue, Taesung Park, Daniel Fremont, Alberto Sangiovanni-Vincentelli, Sanjit Seshia
description: Abstract Safely interacting with humans is a significant challenge for autonomous driving. The performance of this interaction depends on machine learning-based modules of an autopilot, such as perception, behavior prediction, and planning. These modules require training datasets with high-quality labels and a diverse range of realistic dynamic behaviors.

title: A Selective Survey on Versatile Knowledge Distillation Paradigm for Neural Network Models
creator: Jeong-Hoe Ku, JiHun Oh, YoungYoon Lee, Gaurav Pooniwala, SangJeong Lee
description: Abstract This paper aims to provide a selective survey about knowledge distillation (KD) framework for researchers and practitioners to take advantage of it for developing new optimized models in the deep neural network field. To this end, we give a brief overview of knowledge distillation and some related works including learning using privileged information (LUPI) and generalized distillation (GD).

title: Characteristic cycles associated to holonomic 𝒟 \mathscr{D} -modules
creator: Lei Wu
description:
A 2020 arXiv research paper by Lei Wu. We study relative and logarithmic characteristic cycles associated to holonomic 𝒟 \mathscr{D} -modules. As applications, we obtain: (1) an alternative proof of Ginsburg’s log characteristic cycle formula for lattices of regular holonomic 𝒟 \mathscr{D} -modules following ideas of Sabbah and Briancon-Maisonobe-Merle, and (2) the constructibility of the log de Rham complexes for lattices of holonomic 𝒟 \mathscr{D} -modules, which is a natural generalization of Kashiwara’s constructibility theorem. 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification
