description: Abstract We present network embedding algorithms that capture information about a node from the local distribution over node attributes around it, as observed over random walks following an approach similar to Skip-gram. Observations from neighborhoods of different sizes are either pooled (AE) or encoded distinctly in a multi-scale approach (MUSAE).

title: GACNN: Training Deep Convolutional Neural Networks with Genetic Algorithm
creator: Parsa Esfahanian, Mohammad Akhavan
description: Abstract Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have gained a significant attraction in the recent years due to their increasing real-world applications. Their performance is highly dependent to the network structure and the selected optimization method for tuning the network parameters. In this paper, we propose novel yet efficient methods for training convolutional neural networks.

title: Arc length based WENO scheme for Hamilton-Jacobi Equations
creator: Samala Rathan, Biswarup Biswas
description: Abstract In this article, novel smoothness indicators are presented for calculating the nonlinear weights of weighted essentially non-oscillatory scheme to approximate the viscosity numerical solutions of Hamilton-Jacobi equations. These novel smoothness indicators are constructed from the derivatives of reconstructed polynomials over each sub-stencil.

title: Test-Time Training with Self-Supervision for Generalization under Distribution Shifts
creator: Yu Sun, Xiaolong Wang, Zhuang Liu, John Miller, Alexei A. Efros, Moritz Hardt, Yu Sun, Xiaolong Wang, Zhuang Liu, John Miller, Alexei A. Efros, Moritz Hardt
description: Abstract In this paper, we propose Test-Time Training, a general approach for improving the performance of predictive models when training and test data come from different distributions. We turn a single unlabeled test sample into a self-supervised learning problem, on which we update the model parameters before making a prediction. This also extends naturally to data in an online stream.

title: End-to-End Deep Convolutional Active Contours for Image Segmentation
creator: Ali Hatamizadeh, Debleena Sengupta, Demetri Terzopoulos
description: Abstract The Active Contour Model (ACM) is a standard image analysis technique whose numerous variants have attracted an enormous amount of research attention across multiple fields. Incorrectly, however, the ACM’s differential-equation-based formulation and prototypical dependence on user initialization have been regarded as being largely incompatible with the recently popular deep learning approaches to image segmentation.

title: Enhancing Electrical Properties and Seebeck Effects of WO 3 Thin Films Using Spray Pyrolysis: Insights into the Conductivity and Carrier Type
creator: Zahra Asghari, Hamid Arian Zad, Hosein Eshghi
description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Zahra Asghari, Hamid Arian Zad, Hosein Eshghi. This study focuses on enhancing the electrical and thermoelectric properties of tungsten trioxide (WO 3 ) thin films using the spray pyrolysis technique. Three samples, namely A 1 , A 2 , and A 3 , were prepared by depositing the films onto glass substrates at different deposition rates: R 1 = 1 {}_{1}=1 mL/min, R 2 = 3 {}_{2}=3 mL/min, and R 3 = 7 {}_{3}=7 mL/min, respectively.

title: Locally Nilpotent Derivations of Free Algebra of Rank Two This paper is a contribution to the Special Issue on Algebra, Topology, and Dynamics in Interaction in honor of Dmitry Fuchs. The full collection is available at https://www.emis.de/journals/SIGMA/Fuchs.html
creator: Vesselin DRENSKY † and Leonid MAKAR-LIMANOV ‡§
description: Abstract In commutative algebra, if δ \delta is a locally nilpotent derivation of the polynomial algebra K ⁡ [ x 1 , … , x d ] K[x_{1},\ldots,x_{d}] over a field K K of characteristic 0 and w w is a nonzero element of the kernel of δ \delta , then Δ = w ​ δ \Delta=w\delta is also a

title: Higher Rank 𝒁 ^ \boldsymbol{\hat{Z}} and 𝑭 𝑲 \boldsymbol{F_{K}}
creator: Sunghyuk PARK
description: Abstract We study q q -series-valued invariants of 3 3 -manifolds that depend on the choice of a root system G G . This is a natural generalization of the earlier works by Gukov–Pei–Putrov–Vafa [arXiv:1701.06567] and Gukov–Manolescu [arXiv:1904.06057] where they focused on G = SU ⁡ ( 2 ) G={\rm SU}(2) case.

title: Bridging Explicit and Implicit Deep Generative Models via Neural Stein Estimators
creator: Qitian Wu, Rui Gao, Hongyuan Zha
description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Qitian Wu, Rui Gao, Hongyuan Zha. There are two types of deep generative models: explicit and implicit. The former defines an explicit density form that allows likelihood inference; while the latter targets a flexible transformation from random noise to generated samples. While the two classes of generative models have shown great power in many applications, both of them, when used alone, suffer from respective limitations and drawbacks.

title: New Examples of Irreducible Local Diffusion of Hyperbolic PDE’s This paper is a contribution to the Special Issue on Algebra, Topology, and Dynamics in Interaction in honor of Dmitry Fuchs. The full collection is available at https://www.emis.de/journals/SIGMA/Fuchs.html
creator: Victor A. VASSILIEV †‡
description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Victor A. VASSILIEV †‡. Local diffusion of strictly hyperbolic higher-order PDE’s with constant coefficients at all simple singularities of corresponding wavefronts can be explained and recognized by only two local geometrical features of these wavefronts. We radically disprove the obvious conjecture extending this fact to arbitrary singularities: namely, we present examples of diffusion at all non-simple singularity classes of generic wavefronts in odd-dimensional spaces, which are not reducible to diffusion at simple singular points.

title: Performance Analysis of SSHC Rectifiers used in Ultrasonic Wireless Power Transfer
creator: Sijun Du 1
description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Sijun Du 1. One of the key design considerations for biomedical implants is to minimize the system volume while achieving high performance. An attractive approach to power biomedical implants is to use wireless power transfer (WPT) with ultrasound. To receive the ultrasonic energy, a piezoelectric transducer is implemented, which is designed to have the resonance frequency at the frequency of the ultrasonic wave. To extract the received energy from the transducer, an energy rectification circuit is typically required.

title: Multi-classifier prediction of knee osteoarthritis progression from incomplete imbalanced longitudinal data
creator: Paweł Widera a , Paco M.J. Welsing b , Christoph Ladel c , John Loughlin d , Floris P.J.G. Lafeber b , Florence Petit Dop e , Jonathan Larkin f , Harrie Weinans g,h , Ali Mobasheri i,j,k , Jaume Bacardit a
description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Paweł Widera a , Paco M.J. Welsing b , Christoph Ladel c , John Loughlin d , Floris P.J.G. Lafeber b , Florence Petit Dop e , Jonathan Larkin f , Harrie Weinans g,h , Ali Mobasheri i,j,k , Jaume Bacardit a. Conventional inclusion criteria used in osteoarthritis clinical trials are not very effective in selecting patients who would benefit from a therapy being tested. Typically majority of selected patients show no or limited disease progression during a trial period.

title: Simple smoothness indicator WENO-Z scheme for hyperbolic conservation laws
creator: Samala Rathan, G. Naga Raju, Ashlesha A. Bhise
description: Abstract The advantage of WENO-JS5 scheme [ J. Comput. Phys. 1996] over the WENO-LOC scheme [J. Comput. Phys.1994] is that the WENO-LOC nonlinear weights do not achieve the desired order of convergence in smooth monotone regions and at critical points.

title: DNA coding and Gödel numbering
creator: Argyris Nicolaidis
description: Abstract Abstract Evolution consists of distinct stages: cosmological, biological, linguistic. Since biology verges on natural sciences and linguistics, we expect that it shares structures and features from both forms of knowledge. Indeed, in DNA we encounter the biological ”atoms”, the four nucleotide molecules. At the same time these four nucleotides may be considered as the ”letters” of an alphabet.

title: Generating Diverse Story Continuations with Controllable Semantics
creator: Lifu Tu Xiaoan Ding Dong Yu Kevin Gimpel, [1ex] Toyota Technological Institute at Chicago, Chicago, IL, 60637, USA
description: Abstract We propose a simple and effective modeling framework for controlled generation of multiple, diverse outputs. We focus on the setting of generating the next sentence of a story given its context. As controllable dimensions, we consider several sentence attributes, including sentiment, length, predicates, frames, and automatically-induced clusters.

title: Information paradox and corrected thermodynamics for black holes
creator: Ming Zhang
description: Abstract We generally consider that entropy and temperature of a spherically symmetric black hole are corrected by quantum effect. We calculate interior entropy variation of massless scalar field and compare it with corrected Bekenstein-Hawking entropy variation for the evaporating black hole. We find that the corrected ratio between them is greater than the uncorrected one.

title: Domain Adaptation for Semantic Segmentation with Maximum Squares Loss
creator: Minghao Chen, Hongyang Xue, Deng Cai
description: Abstract Deep neural networks for semantic segmentation always require a large number of samples with pixel-level labels, which becomes the major difficulty in their real-world applications. To reduce the labeling cost, unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) approaches are proposed to transfer knowledge from labeled synthesized datasets to unlabeled real-world datasets.

title: Schwinger pair production correction in thermal system
creator: Y. L. Wang, H. B. Sang, B. S. Xie
description: Abstract In this paper, we give formal results of Schwinger pair production correction in thermal systems with external background field by using the evolution operator method of thermo field dynamics, where especially tree level correction of thermal photons is considered with linear response approaches by an effective mass shift.

title: On analytical solutions of the DIS structure functions in the framework of GLR-MQ-ZRS equation
creator: Madhurjya Lalung, Pragyan Phukan, Jayanta K. Sarma
description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Madhurjya Lalung, Pragyan Phukan, Jayanta K. Sarma. We computed the deep inelastic scattering (DIS) structure functions F 2 ​ ( x , Q 2 ) F_{2}(x,Q^{2}) and F L ​ ( x , Q 2 ) F_{L}(x,Q^{2}) in the framework of Gribov-Levin-Ryskin-Mueller-Qiu, Zhu-Ruan-Shen (GLR-MQ-ZRS) equation.

title: Undergraduate Quantum Mechanics: a Numerical Approach using QuTiP
creator: Andrew M.C. Dawes
description: Abstract We present an introduction to the Quantum Toolbox in Python (QuTiP) in the context of an undergraduate quantum mechanics class and potential senior research projects. QuTiP provides ready-to-use definitions of standard quantum states and operators as well as numerous dynamic solvers and tools for visualization.

title: Taylor Polynomials in High Arithmetic Precision as Universal Approximators Thanks: Submitted to the editors DATE.
creator: Nikolaos P. Bakas
description: Abstract Function approximation is a generic process in a variety of computational problems, from data interpolation to the solution of differential equations and inverse problems. In this work, a unified approach for such techniques is demonstrated, by utilizing partial sums of Taylor series in high arithmetic precision.

title: Noncollapsed degeneration of Einstein 4 4 -manifolds, I
creator: Tristan Ozuch
description: Abstract A theorem of Anderson and Bando-Kasue-Nakajima from 1989 states that to compactify the set of normalized Einstein metrics with a lower bound on the volume and an upper bound on the diameter in the Gromov-Hausdorff sense, one has to add singular spaces called Einstein orbifolds, and the singularities form as blow-downs of Ricci-flat ALE spaces.

title: A Gradient Free Neural Network Framework Based on Universal Approximation Theorem
creator: N. P. Bakas, A. Langousis, M. Nicolaou, and S. A. Chatzichristofis
description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by N. P. Bakas, A. Langousis, M. Nicolaou, and S. A. Chatzichristofis. We present a numerical scheme for computation of Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) weights, which stems from the Universal Approximation Theorem, avoiding laborious iterations.

title: PlanAlyzer : Assessing Threats to the Validity of Online Experiments DOI: 10.1145/3360608 Journal: PACMPL Volume: 3 OOPSLA 182 10 CCS: Software and its engineering Scripting languages CCS: Software and its engineering Domain specific languages CCS: Software and its engineering Software testing and d
creator: Emma Tosch, Eytan Bakshy, Emery D. Berger, David D. Jensen, J. Eliot B. Moss
description: Abstract . Online experiments have become a ubiquitous aspect of design and engineering processes within Internet firms. As the scale of experiments has grown, so has the complexity of their design and implementation. In response, firms have developed software frameworks for designing and deploying online experiments.

title: On the anticyclotomic Iwasawa main conjecture for Hilbert modular forms of parallel weights
creator: Haining Wang
description: Abstract . In this article, we study the Iwasawa theory for Hilbert modular forms over the anticyclotomic extension of a CM field. We prove a one sided divisibility result toward the Iwasawa main conjecture. The proof relies on the first and second reciprocity law relating theta elements to Heegner points Euler system.

title: Quantifying Cochlear Implant Users’ Ability for Speaker Identification using CI Auditory Stimuli
description: Abstract Speaker recognition is a biometric modality that uses underlying speech information to determine the identity of the speaker. Speaker Identification (SID) under noisy conditions is one of the challenging topics in the field of speech processing, specifically when it comes to individuals with cochlear implants (CI).

title: Augmenting Music Sheets with Harmonic Fingerprints Conference: ACM Symposium on Document Engineering 2019; September 23–26, 2019; Berlin, Germany ACM Symposium on Document Engineering 2019 (DocEng ’19), September 23–26, 2019, Berlin, Germany Price: 15.00 DOI: 10.1145/3342558.3345395 ISBN: 978-1-4503
creator: Matthias Miller, Alexandra Bonnici, Mennatallah El-Assady
description: Abstract . Common Music Notation (CMN) is the well-established foundation for the written communication of musical information, such as rhythm or harmony. CMN suffers from the complexity of its visual encoding and the need for extensive training to acquire proficiency and legibility. While alternative notations using additional visual variables (e.g.

title: Wilf collapse in permutation classes
creator: Michael Albert, Vít Jelínek, Michal Opler
description: Abstract For a hereditary permutation class 𝒞 {\mathcal{C}} , we say that two permutations π \pi and σ \sigma of 𝒞 {\mathcal{C}} are Wilf-equivalent in 𝒞 {\mathcal{C}} , if 𝒞 {\mathcal{C}} has the same number of permutations avoiding π \pi as those avoiding σ \sigma .

title: Pulse solutions of the fractional effective models of the Fermi-Pasta-Ulam lattice with long-range interactions
creator: Gervais Nazaire Beukam Chendjou, Jean Pierre Nguenang, Andrea Trombettoni, Thierry Dauxois, Ramaz Khomeriki, Stefano Ruffo
description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Gervais Nazaire Beukam Chendjou, Jean Pierre Nguenang, Andrea Trombettoni, Thierry Dauxois, Ramaz Khomeriki, Stefano Ruffo. We study analytical solutions of the Fractional Boussinesq Equation (FBE), which is an effective model for the Fermi-Pasta-Ulam (FPU) one-dimensional lattice with long-range couplings. The couplings decay as a power-law with exponent s s , with 1 < s < 3 1<s<3 , so that the energy density is finite, but s s is small enough to observe genuine long-range effects.

title: Saturn atmospheric dynamics one year after Cassini: Long-lived features and time variations in the drift of the Hexagon Journal: Icarus
creator: R. Hueso, A. Sánchez-Lavega, J. F. Rojas, A. A. Simon, T. Barry, T. del Río-Gaztelurrutia, A. Antuñano, K. M. Sayanagi, M. Delcroix, L.N. Fletcher, E. García-Melendo, S. Pérez-Hoyos, J. Blalock, F. Colas, J. M. Gómez-Forrellad, J. L. Gunnarson, D. Peach, M. H. Wong
description: Abstract We examine Saturn’s atmospheric dynamics with observations in the visible range from ground-based telescopes and Hubble Space Telescope (HST). We present a detailed analysis of observations acquired during 2018 obtaining drift rates of major meteorological systems from the equator to the North polar hexagon.

title: Radio Resource Dimensioning with Cox Process Based User Location Distribution
creator: Ridha Nasri, Jalal Rachad, Laurent Decreusefond
description: Abstract The upcoming fifth generation (5G) New Radio (NR) interface inherits many concepts and techniques from 4G systems such as the Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplex (OFDM) based waveform and multiple access. Dimensioning 5G NR interface will likely follow the same principles as in 4G networks.

title: Towards Races in Linear Logic
creator: Wen Kokke \rsuper a, J. Garrett Morris \rsuper b, Philip Wadler \rsuper a
description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Wen Kokke \rsuper a, J. Garrett Morris \rsuper b, Philip Wadler \rsuper a. Process calculi based in logic, such as πDILL and CP, provide a foundation for deadlock-free concurrent programming, but exclude non-determinism and races. HCP is a reformulation of CP which addresses a fundamental shortcoming: the fundamental operator for parallel composition from the π-calculus does not correspond to any rule of linear logic, and therefore not to any term construct in CP.

title: Existence of solution for Hilfer fractional differential problem with nonlocal boundary condition
creator: Hanan A. Wahash, Mohammed S. Abdo, Satish K. Panchal, Sandeep P. Bhairat
description: Abstract . This paper is devoted to study the existence of a solution to Hilfer fractional differential equation with nonlocal boundary condition. We use the equivalent integral equation to study the considered Hilfer differential problem with nonlocal boundary condition. The Mönch type fixed point theorem and the measure of the noncompactness technique are the main tools in this study.

title: A covariant simultaneous action for branes Journal: .
creator: Riccardo Capovilla and Giovany Cruz
description: Abstract A covariant simultaneous action for branes in an arbitrary curved background spacetime is considered. The action depends on a pair of independent field variables, the brane embedding functions, through the canonical momentum of a reparametrization invariant geometric model for the brane, and an auxiliary vector field. The form of the action is analogous to a symplectic potential.

title: Hidden-charm and hidden-bottom molecular pentaquarks in chiral perturbation theory
creator: Bo Wang, Lu Meng, Shi-Lin Zhu
description: Abstract The newly observed P c ​ ( 4312 ) P_{c}(4312) , P c ​ ( 4440 ) P_{c}(4440) and P c ​ ( 4457 ) P_{c}(4457) at the LHCb experiment are very close to the Σ c ​ D ¯ \Sigma_{c}\bar{D} and Σ c ​ D ¯ ∗ \Sigma_{c}\bar{D}^{\ast} thresholds.

title: Aging transition in the absence of inactive oscillators
creator: K. Sathiyadevi, I. Gowthaman, D. V. Senthilkumar, V. K. Chandrasekar
description: Abstract The role of counter-rotating oscillators in an ensemble of coexisting co- and counter-rotating oscillators is examined by increasing the proportion of the latter. The phenomenon of aging transition was identified at a critical value of the ratio of the counter-rotating oscillators, which was otherwise realized only by increasing the number of inactive oscillators to a large extent.

title: Curiosity-driven Reinforcement Learning for Diverse Visual Paragraph Generation Conference: Proceedings of the 27th ACM International Conference on Multimedia; October 21–25, 2019; Nice, France Proceedings of the 27th ACM International Conference on Multimedia (MM ’19), October 21–25, 2019, Nice, Fr
creator: Yadan Luo † , Zi Huang † , Zheng Zhang † , Ziwei Wang † , Jingjing Li ‡ , Yang Yang ‡
description: Abstract . Visual paragraph generation aims to automatically describe a given image from different perspectives and organize sentences in a coherent way. In this paper, we address three critical challenges for this task in a reinforcement learning setting: the mode collapse, the delayed feedback, and the time-consuming warm-up for policy networks.

title: An Optimal Linear Dynamic Detection Method for Replay Attack in Cyber-Physical Systems
creator: Amir Khazraei, Hamed Kebriaei, Farzad Rajaei Salmasi
description: Abstract The problem of detecting replay attack to the linear stochastic system with Kalman filer state estimator and LQG controller is addressed. To this end, a dynamic attack detector method is proposed which is coupled with the dynamics of the system.

title: Accelerating CNN Training by Pruning Activation Gradients Thanks: This work is supported in part by the National Natural Science Foundation of China (61602022), State Key Laboratory of Software Development Environment (SKLSDE-2018ZX-07), CCF-Tencent IAGR20180101 and the 111 Talent Program B16001.
creator: Xucheng Ye, Pengcheng Dai, Junyu Luo, Xin Guo, Yingjie Qi, Jianlei Yang, Yiran Chen
description: Abstract Sparsification is an efficient approach to accelerate CNN inference, but it is challenging to take advantage of sparsity in training procedure because the involved gradients are dynamically changed. Actually, an important observation shows that most of the activation gradients in back-propagation are very close to zero and only have a tiny impact on weight-updating.

title: Centrality Dependence of Multiplicity Fluctuations in Ion-Ion Collisions from the Beam Energy Scan at FAIR
creator: Anuj Chandra, Bushra Ali and Shakeel Ahmad
description: Abstract Abstract Multiplicity distributions and event-by-event multiplicity fluctuations in AuAu collisions at energies in future heavy-ion experiment at the Facility for Anti-proton and Ion Research ( FAIR ) are investigated. Events corresponding to FAIR energies are simulated in the frame work of Ultra Relativistic Quantum Molecular Dynamics ( URQMD ) model.

title: Existence of solution for Hilfer fractional differential equations with boundary value conditions Thanks: Mathematics Subject Classifications: 34A08, 26A33, 34A12,34A40.
creator: Mohammed S. Abdo, Satish K. Panchal, Sandeep P. Bhairat
description: Abstract In this paper, we consider a class of nonlinear fractional differential equations involving Hilfer derivative with boundary conditions. First, we obtain an equivalent integral for the given boundary value problem in weighted space of continuous functions. Then we obtain the existence results for a given problem under a new approach and minimal assumptions on nonlinear function f f .

title: Chest CT Super-resolution and Domain-adaptation using Memory-efficient 3D Reversible GANs
creator: Tycho F. A. van der Ouderaa, Daniel E. Worrall, Bram van Ginneken
description: Abstract \jmlrpages \midlauthor 1,2 1 2 1 University of Amsterdam, Amsterdam, The Netherlands 2 Diagnostic Image Analysis Group, Radboud UMC, Nijmegen, The Netherlands † † proceedings: MIDL: Medical Imaging with Deep Learning † † year: 2019 † † workshop: MIDL 2019 – Extended Abstract Track 1 Introduction Recently, paired (e.g. Pix2pix Isola et al. 2017 ) and unpaired (e.g.

title: Pseudo-Labeling Curriculum for Unsupervised Domain Adaptation
creator: Jaehoon Choi, Minki Jeong, Taekyung Kim, Changick Kim
description: Abstract To learn target discriminative representations, using pseudo-labels is a simple yet effective approach for unsupervised domain adaptation. However, the existence of false pseudo-labels, which may have a detrimental influence on learning target representations, remains a major challenge. To overcome this issue, we propose a pseudo-labeling curriculum based on a density-based clustering algorithm.

title: Short Star-Products for Filtered Quantizations, I This paper is a contribution to the Special Issue on Algebra, Topology, and Dynamics in Interaction in honor of Dmitry Fuchs. The full collection is available at https://www.emis.de/journals/SIGMA/Fuchs.html
creator: Pavel ETINGOF and Douglas STRYKER
description: Abstract We develop a theory of short star-products for filtered quantizations of graded Poisson algebras, introduced in 2016 by Beem, Peelaers and Rastelli for algebras of regular functions on hyperKähler cones in the context of 3-dimensional N = 4 N=4 superconformal field theories [Beem C., Peelaers W., Rastelli L., Comm. Math. Phys. 354 (2017), 345–392].

title: Reinforcement Learning for Personalized Dialogue Management
creator: Floris den Hengst, Mark Hoogendoorn, Frank van Harmelen, Joost Bosman
description: Abstract Language systems have been of great interest to the research community and have recently reached the mass market through various assistant platforms on the web. Reinforcement Learning methods that optimize dialogue policies have seen successes in past years and have recently been extended into methods that personalize the dialogue, e.g. take the personal context of users into account.

title: Pathological Myopic Image Analysis with Transfer Learning
creator: Ruitao Xie, Libo Liu, Jingxin Liu, Connor S Qiu
description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Ruitao Xie, Libo Liu, Jingxin Liu, Connor S Qiu. We present a summary of transfer learning based methods for several challenging myopic fundus image analysis tasks including classification of pathological and non-pathological myopia, localisation of fovea, and segmentation of optic disc. By adapting existing popular deep learning architectures, our proposed methods have achieved 1st and 2nd place in several tasks at the Pathologic Myopia Challenge (PALM) 1 1 1 https://palm.grand-challenge.org/ held at ISBI2019 .

title: Non-existence of Riemannian metric satisfying Yamabe soliton
creator: Absos Ali Shaikh 1 , Chandan Kumar Mondal 2
description: Abstract . In this paper we have proved that a compact Riemannian manifold does not admit a metric with positive scalar curvature if there exists a real valued function in this manifold which is strictly positive along a geodesic ray satisfying expanding or steady Yamabe soliton.

title: GANs ’N Lungs: improving pneumonia prediction
creator: Tatiana Malygina 1,2, Elena Ericheva \midlotherjointauthor 1, Ivan Drokin \midlotherjointauthor 1
description: Abstract We propose a novel method to improve deep learning model performance on highly-imbalanced tasks. The proposed method is based on CycleGAN to achieve balanced dataset. We show that data augmentation with GAN helps to improve accuracy of pneumonia binary classification task even if the generative network was trained on the same training dataset.

title: Improving localization-based approaches for breast cancer screening exam classification
creator: Thibault Févry 1, Jason Phang 1, Nan Wu 1, S. Gene Kim 2, Linda Moy 2, Kyunghyun Cho 1, Krzysztof J. Geras 2,1
description: Abstract We trained and evaluated a localization-based deep CNN for breast cancer screening exam classification on over 200,000 exams (over 1,000,000 images). Our model achieves an AUC of 0.919 in predicting malignancy in patients undergoing breast cancer screening, reducing the error rate of the baseline Wu et al. 2019a by 23%.

title: A Unified Point-Based Framework for 3D Segmentation
creator: Hung-Yueh Chiang, Yen-Liang Lin, Yueh-Cheng Liu, Winston H. Hsu
description: Abstract 3D point cloud segmentation remains challenging for structureless and textureless regions. We present a new unified point-based framework † † Code is available at https://github.com/ken012git/joint_point_based for 3D point cloud segmentation that effectively optimizes pixel-level features, geometrical structures and global context priors of an entire scene.

title: CloudSat-inferred vertical structure of precipitation over the Antarctic continent
description: Abstract Current global warming is causing significant changes in snowfall in polar regions, directly impacting the mass balance of the ice caps. The only water supply in Antarctica, precipitation, is poorly estimated from surface measurements. The onboard cloud-profiling radar of the CloudSat satellite provided the first real opportunity to estimate precipitation at continental scale.

title: Estimation of Tire-Road Friction for Road Vehicles: a Time Delay Neural Network Approach Journal: Journal of the Brazilian Society of Mechanical Sciences and Engineering
creator: Alexandre M. Ribeiro, Alexandra Moutinho, André R. Fioravanti, Ely C. de Paiva
description: Abstract The performance of vehicle active safety systems is dependent on the friction force arising from the contact of tires and the road surface. Therefore, an adequate knowledge of the tire-road friction coefficient is of great importance to achieve a good performance of different vehicle control systems.

title: Direct and inverse results on restricted signed sumsets in integers Thanks: ∗ Research supported by the Ministry of Human Resource Development, India.
creator: Jagannath Bhanja ∗, Takao Komatsu, Ram Krishna Pandey
description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Jagannath Bhanja ∗, Takao Komatsu, Ram Krishna Pandey. Let G G be an additive abelian group. Let A = { a 0 , a 1 , … , a k − 1 } A=\{a_{0},a_{1},\ldots,a_{k-1}\} be a nonempty finite subset of G G .

title: Assessment of low-altitude atmospheric turbulence models for aircraft aeroelasticity Journal: Journal of Fluids and Structures
creator: Georgios Deskos, Alfonso del Carre, Rafael Palacios
description: Abstract We investigate the dynamic response of flexible aircraft in low-altitude atmospheric turbulence. To this end, three turbulence models of increasing fidelity, namely, the one-dimensional von Kármán model, the two-dimensional Kaimal model and full three-dimensional wind fields extracted from large-eddy simulations (LES) are used to simulate ambient turbulence near the ground.

title: Set-Based Models for Cryptocurrency Software
creator: Gustavo Betarte, Maximiliano Cristiá, Carlos Luna, Adrián Silveira, Dante Zanarini
description: Abstract Emin Gün Sirer once said 1 1 1 hackingdistributed.com/2016/06/17/thoughts-on-the-dao-hack . : It’s clear that writing a robust, secure smart contract requires extreme amounts of diligence. It’s more similar to writing code for a nuclear power reactor, than to writing loose web code […] Yet the current Solidity language and underlying EVM seems designed more for the latter.

title: Cálculo de constantes ópticas de películas delgadas de Silicio compensado a través del método de Swanepoel
creator: W. A. Rojas C, M. Chaparro P, L. M. Pardo C, M. I. Cruz F
description: Abstract Characterization and determination of the optical constants for thin film silicon compensated through the transmittance spectrum is presented. Such properties were determined by R. Swanepoel model. Comparison between the refractive indices of pure silicon and silicon compensated. Increasing refractive index behavior at low wavelengths in both plots was observed.

title: On existence of solution to nonlinear
creator: ψ
description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by ψ. Abstract The aim of this paper is to obtain the existence of unique solution to nonlinear Cauchy-type problem. We consider the implicit nonlinear Cauchy-type problem with \psi- Hilfer fractional derivative. The Banach fixed point theorem is used to obtain the existence of a unique solution whereas the generalized Gronwall inequality is used to discuss continuous data dependence of the solution. The results obtained herein are supported with illustrative example.

title: Feature Robustness in Non-stationary Health Records: Caveats to Deployable Model Performance in Common Clinical Machine Learning Tasks These authors contributed equally, and should be considered co-first authors.
creator: Bret Nestor, Matthew B. A. McDermott, Willie Boag, Gabriela Berner, Tristan Naumann, Michael C. Hughes, Anna Goldenberg, Marzyeh Ghassemi
description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Bret Nestor, Matthew B. A. McDermott, Willie Boag, Gabriela Berner, Tristan Naumann, Michael C. Hughes, Anna Goldenberg, Marzyeh Ghassemi. When training clinical prediction models from electronic health records (EHRs), a key concern should be a model’s ability to sustain performance over time when deployed, even as care practices, database systems, and population demographics evolve.

title: Aquarium: Cassiopea and Alewife Languages (Prerelease Version of 20220108)
creator: David A. Holland, Jingmei Hu, Ming Kawaguchi, Eric Lu, Stephen Chong, Margo I. Seltzer
description: Abstract . This technical report describes two of the domain specific languages used in the Aquarium kernel code synthesis project. It presents the language cores in terms of abstract syntax. Cassiopea is a machine description language for describing the semantics of processor instruction sets.

title: Integrating Spatial Configuration into Heatmap Regression Based CNNs for Landmark Localization
creator: Christian Payer 1,2, Darko Štern 2, Horst Bischof 1, Martin Urschler 2,1
description: Abstract In many medical image analysis applications, often only a limited amount of training data is available, which makes training of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) challenging. In this work on anatomical landmark localization, we propose a CNN architecture that learns to split the localization task into two simpler sub-problems, reducing the need for large training datasets.

title: Measurement of J / ψ J/\psi production in association with a W ± W^{\pm} boson with p ​ p pp data at 8 TeV
creator: The ATLAS Collaboration
description: Abstract A measurement of the production of a prompt J / ψ J/\psi meson in association with a W ± W^{\pm} boson with W ± → μ ​ ν W^{\pm}\rightarrow\mu\nu and J / ψ → μ + ​ μ − J/\psi\rightarrow\mu^{+}\mu^{-} is presented for J / ψ J/\psi transverse momenta in the range 8.5 8.

title: OPTIMAL WINDOWING OF MR IMAGES USING DEEP LEARNING: AN ENABLER FOR ENHANCED VISUALIZATION
creator: Deepthi S, Dheeraj Kulkarni, Jignesh Dholakia
description: Abstract Window width (WW) and window level (WL) adjustments aid in visualizing anatomies with a suitable contrast. However, the presence of background noise in MR images biases the calculation of default WW/WL values since it necessitates a trade-off between enhancing contrast of foreground/anatomy of interest vs suppressing background/ outside the anatomy of interest.

title: Uncertainty Quantification in Computer-Aided Diagnosis: Make Your Model say “I don’t know” for Ambiguous Cases
creator: Max-Heinrich Laves, Sontje Ihler, Tobias Ortmaier
description: Abstract We evaluate two different methods for the integration of prediction uncertainty into diagnostic image classifiers to increase patient safety in deep learning 1 1 1 Code is available at https://github.com/mlaves/uncertainty-midl . In the first method, Monte Carlo sampling is applied with dropout at test time to get a posterior distribution of the class labels (Bayesian ResNet).

title: Secure Calibration for Safety-Critical IoT: Traceability for Safety Resilience
creator: Ryan Shah †, Michael McIntee †, Shishir Nagaraja †, Sahil Bhandary ‡, Prerna Arote ‡, Joy Kuri ‡
description: Abstract Secure sensor calibration constitutes a foundational step that underpins operational safety in the Industrial Internet of Things. While much attention has been given to IoT security such as the use of TLS to secure sensed data, little thought has been given to securing the calibration infrastructure itself.

title: Ground state energy and topological mass in spacetimes with nontrivial topology
creator: Paulo J. Porfírio, Herondy F. Santana Mota, Gabriel Queiroz Garcia
description: Abstract In this paper we study the ground state energy of a massless scalar field and generation of topological mass by considering a quasi-periodically identified Minkowski spacetime and the ‘half-Einstein Universe’, that is, an Einstein Universe where the massless scalar field satisfies the Dirichlet boundary condition.

title: OntoPlot: A Novel Visualisation for Non-hierarchical Associations in Large Ontologies
creator: Ying Yang, Michael Wybrow, Yuan-Fang Li, Tobias Czauderna, Yongqun He
description: Abstract Ontologies are formal representations of concepts and complex relationships among them. They have been widely used to capture comprehensive domain knowledge in areas such as biology and medicine, where large and complex ontologies can contain hundreds of thousands of concepts. Especially due to the large size of ontologies, visualisation is useful for authoring, exploring and understanding their underlying data.

title: Deformable Medical Image Registration Using a Randomly-Initialized CNN as Regularization Prior
creator: Max-Heinrich Laves, Sontje Ihler, Tobias Ortmaier
description: Abstract We present deformable unsupervised medical image registration using a randomly-initialized deep convolutional neural network (CNN) as regularization prior. Conventional registration methods predict a transformation by minimizing dissimilarities between an image pair. The minimization is usually regularized with manually engineered priors, which limits the potential of the registration.

title: The effect of mechanical stress on lithium distribution and geometry optimisation for multi-material lithium-ion anodes. Journal: Journal of The Electrochemical Society
creator: Ian P. E. Roper a , ∗ {}^{\text{a},*} , S. Jon Chapman b,c {}^{\text{b,c}} , Colin P. Please b,c {}^{\text{b,c}}
description: Abstract A model is presented for predicting the open-circuit voltage (OCV) and lithium distribution within lithium-ion anodes containing multiple materials, coupling linear elasticity with a stress-dependent chemical potential. The model is applied to a spherical radially-symmetric nano-particle with a silicon core and a graphite shell, highlighting the large effect on lithium distribution and OCV caused by the stress-coupling.

title: Active Matter Invasion amin.doostmohammadi@physics.ox.ac.uk
creator: Felix Kempf, Romain Mueller, Erwin Frey, Julia M. Yeomans, Amin Doostmohammadi
description: Abstract Biological active materials such as bacterial biofilms and eukaryotic cells thrive in confined micro-spaces. Here, we show through numerical simulations that confinement can serve as a mechanical guidance to achieve distinct modes of collective invasion when combined with growth dynamics and the intrinsic activity of biological materials.

title: Deep learning for automatic tumour segmentation in PET/CT images of patients with head and neck cancers
creator: Yngve Mardal Moe 1, Aurora Rosvoll Groendahl 1, Martine Mulstad 1, Oliver Tomic 1, Ulf Indahl 1, Einar Dale 2, Eirik Malinen 3,4, Cecilia Marie Futsaether 1
description: Abstract An automatic segmentation algorithm for delineation of the gross tumour volume and pathologic lymph nodes of head and neck cancers in PET/CT images is described. The proposed algorithm is based on a convolutional neural network using the U-Net architecture.

title: Isospin-Violating Dark Matter in the U ​ ( 1 ) ′ U(1)^{\prime} Model Inspired by E 6 E_{6}
creator: Tianjun Li, Qian-Fei Xiang, Qi-Shu Yan, Xianhui Zhang, Han Zhou
description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Tianjun Li, Qian-Fei Xiang, Qi-Shu Yan, Xianhui Zhang, Han Zhou. We propose a U ​ ( 1 ) ′ U(1)^{\prime} model inspired by E 6 E_{6} which has an isospin-violation dark matter. With extra two pairs of vector-like quarks, we can assign the proper U ​ ( 1 ) ′ U(1)^{\prime} charges for the first two-generation quark doublets, and explain why the first two-generation quarks are lighter than the third generation.

title: Multilinear fractional integral operators: a counter-example Thanks: Key words and phrases : Multilinear Fractional Operators, Hardy Spaces. Thanks: 2.010 Math. Subject Classification : 42B20, 42B30.
creator: Pablo Rocha
description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Pablo Rocha. By means of a counter-example we show that the multilinear fractional operator ℐ γ \mathcal{I}_{\gamma} ( 1 < γ < 2 1<\gamma<2 ) is not bounded from H 1 ​ ( ℝ ) × H p ​ ( ℝ ) H^{1}(\mathbb{R})\times H^{p}(\mathbb{R}) into H q ​ ( ℝ ) H^{q}(\mathbb{R}) , for 0 < p ≤ γ − 1 0<p\leq\gamma^{-1} and 1 q = 1 + 1 p − γ \frac{1}{q}=1+\frac{1}{p}-\gamma .

title: A parametrization of 8 × 8 8\times 8 magic squares of squares through octonionic multiplication
creator: Ísabel Pirsic
description: Abstract In 1771 Euler posed what he called a ‘problema curiosum’ [ 3 ] : to find a 4\times 4 magic square of squares, i.e., an integer matrix M such that MM^{\top}=M^{\top}M=c*I,\ c\in\mathbb{Z} , where also the sums of the squares of the diagonal entries should add up to c . He gave explicit solutions, e.g.

title: Uncertainty Propagation in a Multiscale CALPHAD-Reinforced Elastochemical Phase-field Model Journal: TexExchange Journal: Journal of L a T e X Templates
creator: Vahid Attari a,∗, Pejman Honarmandi a, Thien Duong a, Daniel J Sauceda a, Douglas Allaire b, Raymundo Arroyave a,b
description: Abstract ICME approaches provide decision support for materials design by establishing quantitative process-structure-property relations. Confidence in the decision support, however, must be achieved by establishing uncertainty bounds in ICME model chains. The quantification and propagation of uncertainty in computational materials science, however, remains a rather unexplored aspect of computational materials science approaches.

title: Large finite products of small fractions Thanks: This work was partially supported by Conselho Nacional de Desenvolvimento Científico e Tecnológico – CNPq (Proc. 423833/2018-9).
creator: Arnaldo Mandel
description: Abstract . Fix positive reals a , b , c , d a,b,c,d , and let h ⁡ ( x ) h(x) be a real function behaving sort of like sin ⁡ x \sin x near 0. Then, provided m m grows linearly with n n .

title: A Topological Data Analysis Perspective on Non-Covalent Interactions in Relativistic Calculations
creator: Małgorzata Olejniczak, André Severo Pereira Gomes, Julien Tierny
description: Abstract Topological Data Analysis (TDA) is a powerful mathematical theory, largely unexplored in theoretical chemistry. In this work we demonstrate how TDA provides new insights into topological features of electron densities and reduced density gradients, by investigating the effects of relativity on the bonding of the Au 4 -S-C 6 H 4 -S’-Au’ 4 molecule.

title: AutoML: A Survey of the State-of-the-Art Journal: Knowledge-Based Systems
creator: Xin He, Kaiyong Zhao, Xiaowen Chu
description: Abstract Deep learning (DL) techniques have obtained remarkable achievements on various tasks, such as image recognition, object detection, and language modeling. However, building a high-quality DL system for a specific task highly relies on human expertise, hindering its wide application.

title: A Multi-Media Exchange Format for Time-Series Dataset Curation
creator: Philipp M. Scholl, Benjamin Völker, Bernd Becker, Kristof Van Laerhoven
description: Abstract Exchanging data as character-separated values (CSV) is slow, cumbersome and error-prone. Especially for time-series data, which is common in Activity Recognition, synchronizing several independently recorded sensors is challenging. Adding second level evidence, like video recordings from multiple angles and time-coded annotations, further complicates the matter of curating such data.

title: The Impact of Time on Hashtag Reuse in Twitter: A Cognitive-Inspired Hashtag Recommendation Approach
creator: Elisabeth Lex, Dominik Kowald
description: Abstract In our work [ kowald2017www ] , we study temporal usage patterns of Twitter hashtags, and we use the Base-Level Learning (BLL) equation from the cognitive architecture ACT-R [ anderson2004integrated ] to model how a person reuses her own, individual hashtags as well as hashtags from her social network.

title: Observations of radio sources near the Sun
creator: O. Titov, S. Lambert, B. Soja, F. Shu, A. Melnikov, J. McCallum, L. McCallum, M. Schartner, A. de Witt, D. Ivanov, A. Mikhailov, S. O. Yi, W. Chen, B. Xia, M. Ishigaki, S. Gulyaev, T. Natusch, S. Weston
description: Abstract Geodetic Very Long Baseline Interferometry (VLBI) data are capable of measuring the light deflection caused by the gravitational field of the Sun and large planets with high accuracy. The parameter γ \gamma of the parametrized Post-Newtonian (PPN) formalism estimated using observations of reference radio sources near the Sun should be equal to unity in the general relativity.

title: Predicting Behavior in Cancer-Afflicted Patient and Spouse Interactions using Speech and Language
description: Abstract Cancer impacts the quality of life of those diagnosed as well as their spouse caregivers, in addition to potentially influencing their day-to-day behaviors. There is evidence that effective communication between spouses can improve well-being related to cancer but it is difficult to efficiently evaluate the quality of daily life interactions using manual annotation frameworks.

title: Electron and photon performance measurements with the ATLAS detector using the 2015–2017 LHC proton–proton collision data
creator: The ATLAS Collaboration
description: Abstract This paper describes the reconstruction of electrons and photons with the ATLAS detector, employed for measurements and searches exploiting the complete LHC Run 2 dataset. An improved energy clustering algorithm is introduced, and its implications for the measurement and identification of prompt electrons and photons are discussed in detail.

title: Visualization of Abel’s Impossibility Theorem
creator: Veronica Kalicki, Juan Morales, Ryan Ostrander
description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Veronica Kalicki, Juan Morales, Ryan Ostrander. In this paper we construct a visualization of the Abel’s Impossibility Theorem also known as the Abel-Ruffini Theorem. Using the canvas object in JavaScript along with the p5.js library, and given any expression that uses analytic functions and radicals one can always construct closed paths such that the expression evaluated at the coefficients of a general polynomial returns to it’s initial position, while the roots of the polynomial undergo a non-trivial permutation.

title: A Caching Strategy Towards Maximal D2D Assisted Offloading Gain
creator: Yijin Pan, Cunhua Pan, Zhaohui Yang, Ming Chen, Jiangzhou Wang
description: Abstract Device-to-Device (D2D) communications incorporated with content caching have been regarded as a promising way to offload the cellular traffic data. In this paper, the caching strategy is investigated to maximize the D2D offloading gain with the comprehensive consideration of user collaborative characteristics as well as the physical transmission conditions.

title: Adversarially Trained Convolutional Neural Networks for Semantic Segmentation of Ischaemic Stroke Lesion using Multisequence Magnetic Resonance Imaging
creator: Rachana Sathish, Ronnie Rajan, Anusha Vupputuri, Nirmalya Ghosh, Debdoot Sheet
description: Abstract Ischaemic stroke is a medical condition caused by occlusion of blood supply to the brain tissue thus forming a lesion. A lesion is zoned into a core associated with irreversible necrosis typically located at the center of the lesion, while reversible hypoxic changes in the outer regions of the lesion are termed as the penumbra.

title: ADN: Artifact Disentanglement Network for Unsupervised Metal Artifact Reduction Thanks: H. Liao and J. Luo is with the Department of Computer Science, University of Rochester, Rochester, NY, USA (email: hliao6@cs.rochester.edu). Thanks: W. Lin is with the Department of Electrical and Computer Engine
creator: Haofu Liao, Wei-An Lin
description: Abstract Current deep neural network based approaches to computed tomography (CT) metal artifact reduction (MAR) are supervised methods that rely on synthesized metal artifacts for training. However, as synthesized data may not accurately simulate the underlying physical mechanisms of CT imaging, the supervised methods often generalize poorly to clinical applications.

title: On mixed- ω \omega -sheaves
creator: Osamu Fujino
description: Abstract . We introduce the notion of mixed- ω \omega -sheaves and use it for the study of a relative version of Fujita’s freeness conjecture. It is related to the Iitaka conjecture. We note that the notion of mixed- ω \omega -sheaves is a generalization of that of Nakayama’s ω \omega -sheaves in some sense.

title: Optimal Separation and Strong Direct Sum for Randomized Query Complexity
creator: Eric Blais, Joshua Brody
description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Eric Blais, Joshua Brody. We establish two results regarding the query complexity of bounded-error randomized algorithms. Bounded-error separation theorem. There exists a total function f : { 0 , 1 } n → { 0 , 1 } f:\{0,1\}^{n}\to\{0,1\} whose ϵ \epsilon -error randomized query complexity satisfies R ¯ ε ​ ( f ) = Ω ⁡ ( R ⁡ ( f ) ⋅ log ⁡ 1 ϵ ) \overline{\mathrm{R}}_{\varepsilon}(f)=\Omega(\mathrm{R}(f)\cdot\log\frac{1}{\epsilon}) . Strong direct sum theorem.

title: A note on the paper ”Tang et al. [Bull Iran Math Soc (2019) doi:10.1007/s41980-019-00262-y]”
creator: Mohammad Mahdi Motamedinezhad and Rahim Kargar ∗
description: Abstract . Very recently Tang et al. [Bull Iran Math Soc (2019) doi:10.1007/s41980-019-00262-y] have studied some majorization results for two certain subclasses of the starlike functions associated with the sine and cosine functions defined by 𝒮 s ∗ \mathcal{S}^{*}_{s} and 𝒮 c ∗ \mathcal{S}^{*}_{c} , respectively.

title: Non-Abelian Gauge-Invariant Cellular Automata
creator: Pablo Arrighi, Giuseppe Di Molfetta, Nathanaël Eon
description: Abstract Gauge-invariance is a mathematical concept that has profound implications in Physics—as it provides the justification of the fundamental interactions. It was recently adapted to the Cellular Automaton (CA) framework, in a restricted case. In this paper, this treatment is generalized to non-abelian gauge-invariance, including the notions of gauge-equivalent theories and gauge-invariants of configurations.

title: Separating Argument Structure from Logical Structure in AMR
creator: Johan Bos
description: Abstract The AMR (Abstract Meaning Representation) formalism for representing meaning of natural language sentences puts emphasis on predicate-argument structure and was not designed to deal with scope and quantifiers. By extending AMR with indices for contexts and formulating constraints on these contexts, a formalism is derived that makes correct predictions for inferences involving negation and bound variables.

title: A non-equilibrium theoretical framework for statistical physics with application to turbulent systems and their predictability
creator: Richard Kleeman
description: Abstract . A new theoretical approach to non-equilibrium statistical systems has recently been proposed by the author, a co-author and others. It is based on a variational principle which is associated with the discrepancy of a path through thermodynamical space to one following Liouvillean evolution.

title: Seismic Signatures of Stellar Magnetic Activity — What Can We Expect from TESS?
creator: René Kiefer 1,∗ , Anne-Marie Broomhall 1 , Warrick H. Ball 2,3
description: Abstract Asteroseismic methods offer a means to investigate stellar activity and activity cycles as well as to identify those properties of stars which are crucial for the operation of stellar dynamos. With data from CoRoT and Kepler , signatures of magnetic activity have been found in the seismic properties of a few dozen stars.

title: Quantale semantics of Lambek calculus with subexponential modalities
creator: Daniel Rogozin
description: Abstract In this paper, we consider the polymodal version of Lambek calculus with subexponential modalities initially introduced by Kanovich, Kuznetsov, Nigam, and Scedrov [ 10 ] and its quantale semantics. In our approach, subexponential modalities have an interpretation in terms of quantic conuclei. We show that this extension of Lambek calculus is complete w.r.t quantales with quantic conuclei.

title: Search for heavy Higgs bosons decaying to a top quark pair in proton-proton collisions at s = 13 \sqrt{s}=13 \TeV
description: Abstract A search is presented for additional scalar ( \PH ) or pseudoscalar ( \PSA ) Higgs bosons decaying to a top quark pair in proton-proton collisions at a center-of-mass energy of 13 \TeV . The data set analyzed corresponds to an integrated luminosity of 35.9 \fbinv collected by the CMS experiment at the LHC.

title: Shadow Detection for Ultrasound Images Using Unlabeled Data and Synthetic Shadows
creator: Suguru Yasutomi 1,2, Tatsuya Arakaki 3, Ryuji Hamamoto 4,5
description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Suguru Yasutomi 1,2, Tatsuya Arakaki 3, Ryuji Hamamoto 4,5. \jmlrpages \midlauthor 1 Artificial Intelligence Laboratory, Fujitsu Laboratories Ltd. 2 RIKEN AIP-Fujitsu Collaboration Center, RIKEN 3 Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology, Showa University School of Medicine 4 Cancer Translational Research Team, AIP Center, RIKEN 5 Division of Molecular Modification and Cancer Biology, National Cancer Center Research Institute † † proceedings: MIDL: Medical Imaging with Deep Learning † † year: 2019 † † workshop: MIDL 2019 – Extended Abstract Track 1 Introduction Medical ultrasound is a

title: Notes on the norm of pre-Schwarzian derivatives on bi-univalent functions of order α \alpha
creator: H. Mahzoon and R. Kargar
description: Abstract . In the present paper we estimate the norm of the pre-Schwarzian derivative of bi-starlike functions of order α \alpha where α ∈ [ 0 , 1 ) \alpha\in[0,1) . Initially this problem was handled by Rahmatan et al. in [Bull Iran Math Soc 43 : 1037-1043, 2017].

title: Fully Automatic Binary Glioma Grading based on Pre-Therapy MRI using 3D Convolutional Neural Networks
creator: Milan Decuyper, Roel Van Holen
description: Abstract The optimal treatment strategy of newly diagnosed glioma is strongly influenced by tumour malignancy. Manual non-invasive grading based on MRI is not always accurate and biopsies to verify diagnosis negatively impact overall survival. In this paper, we propose a fully automatic 3D computer-aided diagnosis (CAD) system to non-invasively differentiate high-grade glioblastoma from lower-grade glioma.

title: Beyond English-Only Reading Comprehension: Experiments in Zero-Shot Multilingual Transfer for Bulgarian
creator: Momchil Hardalov, Ivan Koychev, Preslav Nakov
description: Abstract Recently, reading comprehension models achieved near-human performance on large-scale datasets such as SQuAD, CoQA, MS Macro, RACE, etc. This is largely due to the release of pre-trained contextualized representations such as BERT and ELMo, which can be fine-tuned for the target task.

title: Designing arbitrary one-dimensional potentials on an atom chip Journal: oe
creator: Mohammadamin Tajik, \authormark 1 Bernhard Rauer, \authormark 1,2 Thomas Schweigler, \authormark 1 Federica Cataldini, \authormark 1 João Sabino, \authormark 1,3,4 Frederik S. Møller, \authormark 1 Si-Cong Ji, \authormark 1 Igor E. Mazets, \authormark 1,5 and Jörg Schmiedmayer \authormark 1,*
description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Mohammadamin Tajik, \authormark 1 Bernhard Rauer, \authormark 1,2 Thomas Schweigler, \authormark 1 Federica Cataldini, \authormark 1 João Sabino, \authormark 1,3,4 Frederik S. Møller, \authormark 1 Si-Cong Ji, \authormark 1 Igor E. Mazets, \authormark 1,5 and Jörg Schmiedmayer \authormark 1,*. title: Heuristic Algorithm for Generalized Function Matching
creator: Radu Stefan Mincu
description: Abstract The problem of generalized function matching can be defined as follows: given a pattern p = p 1 ⋯ p m p=p_{1}\cdots p_{m} and a text t = t 1 ⋯ t n t=t_{1}\cdots t_{n} , find a mapping f : Σ p → Σ t ∗ f:\Sigma_{p}\rightarrow\Sigma_{t}^{*} and all text locations i i such that f ( p

title: Noncollapsed degeneration of Einstein 4 4 -manifolds, II
creator: Tristan Ozuch
description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Tristan Ozuch. In this second article, we prove that any desingularization in the Gromov-Hausdorff sense of an Einstein orbifold by smooth Einstein metrics is the result of a gluing-perturbation procedure that we develop. This builds on our first paper where we proved that a Gromov-Hausdorff convergence implied a much stronger convergence in suitable weighted Hölder spaces, in which the analysis of the present paper takes place.

title: Generalized Threshold Factorization with Full Collinear Dynamics Preprint: DESY 19-135 NIKHEF 2019-021
creator: Gillian Lustermans, Johannes K. L. Michel, Frank J. Tackmann
description: Abstract Soft threshold factorization has been used extensively to study hadronic collisions. It is derived in the limit where the momentum fractions x a , b x_{a,b} of both incoming partons approach x a , b → 1 x_{a,b}\to 1 .

title: Random Tensors and their Normal Distributions
creator: Changqing Xu, Kaijie Xu
description: Abstract The main purpose of this paper is to introduce the random tensor with normal distribution, which promotes the matrix normal distribution to a higher order case. Some basic knowledge on tensors are introduced before we focus on the random tensors whose entries follow normal distribution.

title: Flat Metrics with a Prescribed Derived Coframing
creator: Robert L. BRYANT † and Jeanne N. CLELLAND ‡
description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Robert L. BRYANT † and Jeanne N. CLELLAND ‡. The following problem is addressed: A 3 3 -manifold M M is endowed with a triple Ω = ( Ω 1 , Ω 2 , Ω 3 ) \Omega=\big(\Omega^{1},\Omega^{2},\Omega^{3}\big) of closed 2 2 -forms.

title: A sceptical analysis of Quantized Inertia 2019 A sceptical analysis of Quantized Inertia – References
creator: Michele Renda
description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Michele Renda. We perform an analysis of the derivation of Quantized Inertia (QI) theory, formerly known with the acronym MiHsC, as presented by McCulloch 2007 ; McCulloch 2013 . Two major flaws were found in the original derivation. We derive a discrete black-body radiation spectrum, deriving a different formulation for F ⁡ ( a ) F(a) than the one presented in the original theory. We present a numerical result of the new solution which is compared against the original prediction.

title: Review of Algorithms for Compressive Sensing of Images
creator: Yoni Sher
description: Abstract We provide a comprehensive review of classical algorithms for compressive sensing of images, focused on Total variation methods, with a view to application in LiDAR systems. Our primary focus is providing a full review for beginners in the field, as well as simulating the kind of noise found in real LiDAR systems.

title: The HiSPARC Experiment Journal: Nuclear Instruments and Methods in Physics Research A
creator: K. van Dam, B. van Eijk, D.B.R.A. Fokkema, J.W. van Holten, A.P.L.S. de Laat, N.G. Schultheiss, J.J.M. Steijger, J.C. Verkooijen
description: Abstract The High School Project on Astrophysics Research with Cosmics (HiSPARC) is a large extensive air shower (EAS) array with detection stations throughout the Netherlands, United Kingdom, Denmark and Namibia. HiSPARC is a collaboration of universities, scientific institutes and high schools. The majority of detection stations is hosted by high schools.

title: Characterising complex healthcare systems using network science: The small world of emergency surgery
creator: Katharina Kohler, Ari Ercole
description: Abstract Hospitals are complex systems and optimising their function is critical to the provision of high quality, cost effective healthcare. Nevertheless, metrics of performance have to date focused on the performance of individual elements rather than the system as a whole.

title: Optimal measures for 𝒑 \boldsymbol{p} -frame energies on spheres
creator: Dmitriy Bilyk, Alexey Glazyrin, Ryan Matzke, Josiah Park, Oleksandr Vlasiuk
description: Abstract . We provide new answers about the placement of mass on spheres so as to minimize energies of pairwise interactions. We find optimal measures for the p p -frame energies, i.e. energies with the kernel given by the absolute value of the inner product raised to a positive power p p .

title: Probabilistic Permutation Invariant Training for Speech Separation
description: Abstract Single-microphone, speaker-independent speech separation is normally performed through two steps: (i) separating the specific speech sources, and (ii) determining the best output-label assignment to find the separation error. The second step is the main obstacle in training neural networks for speech separation.

title: On Complex Gamma-Function Integrals This paper is a contribution to the Special Issue on Elliptic Integrable Systems, Special Functions and Quantum Field Theory. The full collection is available at https://www.emis.de/journals/SIGMA/elliptic-integrable-systems.html
creator: Sergey É. DERKACHOV † and Alexander N. MANASHOV ‡†
description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Sergey É. DERKACHOV † and Alexander N. MANASHOV ‡†. It was observed recently that relations between matrix elements of certain operators in the SL ⁡ ( 2 , ℝ ) {\rm SL}(2,\mathbb{R}) spin chain models take the form of multidimensional integrals derived by R.A. The spin magnets with SL ⁡ ( 2 , ℂ ) {\rm SL}(2,\mathbb{C}) symmetry group and L 2 ​ ( ℂ ) {\rm L}_{2}(\mathbb{C}) as a local Hilbert space give rise to a new type of Γ \Gamma -function integrals.

title: The tunnel number of all 11 and 12 crossing alternating knots Thanks: 2016 Mathematics Subject Classification . 57M25, 57M27
creator: Felipe Castellano-Macías, Nicholas Owad
description: Abstract . Using exhaustive techniques and results from Lackenby and many others, we compute the tunnel number of all 1655 alternating 11 and 12 crossing knots and of 881 non-alternating 11 and 12 crossing knots. We also find all 5525 Montesinos knots with 14 crossings or fewer. 1.

title: Modular Construction of Free Hyperplane Arrangements This paper is a contribution to the Special Issue on Primitive Forms and Related Topics in honor of Kyoji Saito for his 77th birthday. The full collection is available at https://www.emis.de/journals/SIGMA/Saito.html
creator: Shuhei TSUJIE
description: Abstract In this article, we study freeness of hyperplane arrangements. One of the most investigated arrangement is a graphic arrangement. Stanley proved that a graphic arrangement is free if and only if the corresponding graph is chordal and Dirac showed that a graph is chordal if and only if the graph is obtained by “gluing” complete graphs.

title: Understanding the transition from paroxysmal to persistent atrial fibrillation from micro-anatomical re-entry in a simple model
creator: Alberto Ciacci 1,2,4,∗, Max Falkenberg 1,2,4,∗, Kishan A. Manani 1,2,3, Tim S. Evans 1,2, Nicholas S. Peters 4, Kim Christensen 1,2,4
description: Abstract Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common cardiac arrhytmia, characterised by the chaotic motion of electrical wavefronts in the atria. In clinical practice, AF is classified under two primary categories: paroxysmal AF, short intermittent episodes separated by periods of normal electrical activity, and persistent AF, longer uninterrupted episodes of chaotic electrical activity.

title: Evaluating Pest Management Strategies: A Robust Method and Its Application to Strawberry Disease Management Thanks: Selected paper prepared for presentation at the 2019 Agricultural & Applied Economics Association Annual Meeting, Atlanta, GA, July 21-23.
creator: Ariel Soto-Caro, Feng Wu, Zhengfei Guan, Natalia Peres
description: Abstract Farmers use pesticides to reduce yield losses. The efficacies of pesticide treatments are often evaluated by analyzing the average treatment effects and risks. The stochastic efficiency with respect to a function is often employed in such evaluations through ranking the certainty equivalents of each treatment.

title: Measurement of the average very forward energy as a function of the track multiplicity at central pseudorapidities in proton-proton collisions at s = 13 ​ \TeV \sqrt{s}=13\TeV
description: Abstract The average total energy as well as its hadronic and electromagnetic components are measured with the CMS detector at pseudorapidities − 6.6 < η < − 5.2 -6.6<\eta<-5.2 in proton-proton collisions at a centre-of-mass energy s = 13 ​ \TeV \sqrt{s}=13\TeV .

title: Addressing multiple bit/symbol errors in DRAM subsystem
creator: Ravikiran Yeleswarapu and Arun K. Somani
description: Abstract As DRAM technology continues to evolve towards smaller feature sizes and increased densities, faults in DRAM subsystem are becoming more severe. Current servers mostly use CHIPKILL based schemes to tolerate up-to one/two symbol errors per DRAM beat. Multi-symbol errors arising due to faults in multiple data buses and chips may not be detected by these schemes.

title: ASNets: Deep Learning for Generalised Planning
creator: Sam Toyer sdt@berkeley.edu, Sylvie Thiébaux sylvie.thiebaux@anu.edu.au
description: Abstract In this paper, we discuss the learning of generalised policies for probabilistic and classical planning problems using Action Schema Networks (ASNets). The ASNet is a neural network architecture that exploits the relational structure of (P)PDDL planning problems to learn a common set of weights that can be applied to any problem in a domain.

title: Sparsity Emerges Naturally in Neural Language Models
creator: Naomi Saphra, Adam Lopez
description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Naomi Saphra, Adam Lopez. Concerns about interpretability, computational resources, and principled inductive priors have motivated efforts to engineer sparse neural models for NLP tasks. If sparsity is important for NLP, might well-trained neural models naturally become roughly sparse? Using the Taxi-Euclidean norm to measure sparsity, we find that frequent input words are associated with concentrated or sparse activations, while frequent target words are associated with dispersed activations but concentrated gradients.

title: Explicit Characterization of Performance of a Class of Networked Linear Control Systems
creator: Hossein K. Mousavi, Nader Motee
description: Abstract We show that the steady-state variance as a performance measure for a class of networked linear control systems is expressible as the summation of a rational function over the Laplacian eigenvalues of the network graph. Moreover, we characterize the role of connectivity thresholds for the feedback (and observer) gain design of these networks.

title: Model reduction for coupled free flow over porous media: a hybrid dimensional pore network model approach Journal: Journal of Computational Physics
creator: Kilian Weishaupt, Alexandros Terzis, Ioannis Zarikos, Guang Yang, Matthijs de Winter, Rainer Helmig
description: Abstract Modeling coupled systems of free flow adjacent to a porous medium by means of fully resolved Navier-Stokes equations is limited by the immense computational cost and is thus only feasible for relatively small domains. Model reduction allows to decrease a model’s complexity while maintaining an acceptable degree of accuracy.

title: Local versus Global Strategies in Social Query Expansion
creator: Omar Alonso, Vasileios Kandylas, Serge-Eric Tremblay
description: Abstract . Link sharing in social media can be seen as a collaboratively retrieved set of documents for a query or topic expressed by a hashtag. Temporal information plays an important role for identifying the correct context for which such annotations are valid for retrieval purposes.

title: DLGNet: A Transformer-based Model for Dialogue Response Generation
creator: Oluwatobi O. Olabiyi, Erik T. Mueller
description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Oluwatobi O. Olabiyi, Erik T. Mueller. Neural dialogue models, despite their successes, still suffer from lack of relevance, diversity, and in many cases coherence in their generated responses. These issues can attributed to reasons including (1) short-range model architectures that capture limited temporal dependencies, (2) limitations of the maximum likelihood training objective, (3) the concave entropy profile of dialogue datasets resulting in short and generic responses, and (4) the out-of-vocabulary problem leading to generation of a large number of < < UNK > >

title: Search for dark matter particles produced in association with a Higgs boson in proton-proton collisions at s = 13 ​ \TeV \sqrt{s}=13\TeV
description: Abstract A search for dark matter (DM) particles is performed using events with a Higgs boson candidate and large missing transverse momentum. The analysis is based on proton-proton collision data at a center-of-mass energy of 13 \TeV collected by the CMS experiment at the LHC in 2016, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 35.9 \fbinv .

title: Counting rational points of a Grassmannian
creator: Seungki Kim
description: Abstract . We prove an estimate on the number of rational points on the Grassmannian variety of bounded twisted height, refining the classical results of Schmidt ( [ 12 ] ) and Thunder ( [ 20 ] ) over the rational field: most importantly, our formula counts all points.

title: REAPS: Towards Better Recognition of Fine-grained Images by Region Attending and Part Sequencing
creator: Peng Zhang, Xinyu Zhu, Zhanzhan Cheng, Shuigeng Zhou, Yi Niu
description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Peng Zhang, Xinyu Zhu, Zhanzhan Cheng, Shuigeng Zhou, Yi Niu. Fine-grained image recognition has been a hot research topic in computer vision due to its various applications. The-state-of-the-art is the part/region-based approaches that first localize discriminative parts/regions, and then learn their fine-grained features.

title: In-orbit demonstration of X-ray pulsar navigation with the Insight -HXMT satellite
creator: S. J. Zheng 1 , S. N. Zhang 1,2 , F. J. Lu 1,2 , W. B. Wang 3 , Y. Gao 3 , T. P. Li 1,2,4 , L. M. Song 1,2 , M. Y. Ge 1 , D. W. Han 1 , Y. Chen 1 , Y. P. Xu 1 , X. L. Cao 1 , C. Z. Liu 1 , S. Zhang 1,2 , J. L. Qu 1,2 , Z. Chang 1 , G. Chen 1 , L. Chen 5 , T. X. Chen 1 , Y. B. Chen 4 , Y. P. Chen 1 ,
description: Abstract In this work, we report the in-orbit demonstration of X-ray pulsar navigation with Insight -Hard X-ray Modulation Telescope ( Insight -HXMT), which was launched on Jun. 15 th , 2017. The new pulsar navigation method ‘Significance Enhancement of Pulse-profile with Orbit-dynamics’ (SEPO) is adopted to determine the orbit with observations of only one pulsar.

title: The QCD Axion and Unification
creator: Pavel Fileviez Pérez, Clara Murgui, and Alexis D. Plascencia
description: Abstract The QCD axion is one of the most appealing candidates for the dark matter in the Universe. In this article, we discuss the possibility to predict the axion mass in the context of a simple renormalizable grand unified theory where the Peccei-Quinn scale is determined by the unification scale.

title: Omni SCADA Intrusion Detection Using Deep Learning Algorithms
creator: Jun Gao, Luyun Gan, Fabiola Buschendorf, Liao Zhang, Hua Liu, Peixue Li, Xiaodai Dong, Tao Lu
description: Abstract We investigate deep learning based omni intrusion detection system (IDS) for supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) networks that are capable of detecting both temporally uncorrelated and correlated attacks. Regarding the IDSs developed in this paper, a feedforward neural network (FNN) can detect temporally uncorrelated attacks at an F 1 of 99.967 ± {\pm} 0.

title: The Use of Binary Choice Forests to Model and Estimate Discrete Choices
creator: Ningyuan Chen, Guillermo Gallego, Zhuodong Tang
description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Ningyuan Chen, Guillermo Gallego, Zhuodong Tang. In retailing, discrete choice models (DCMs) are commonly used to capture the choice behavior of customers when offered an assortment of products. When estimating DCMs using transaction data, flexible models (such as machine learning models or nonparametric models) are typically not interpretable and hard to estimate, while tractable models (such as the multinomial logit model) tend to misspecify the complex behavior represeted in the data.

title: Characterizations of the Hardy space ℋ F ​ I ​ O 1 ​ ( ℝ n ) \mathcal{H}_{FIO}^{1}(\mathbb{R}^{n}) for Fourier Integral Operators
creator: Zhijie Fan, Naijia Liu, Jan Rozendaal and Liang Song
description: Abstract . The Hardy spaces for Fourier integral operators ℋ F ​ I ​ O p ​ ( ℝ n ) \mathcal{H}_{FIO}^{p}(\mathbb{R}^{n}) , for 1 ≤ p ≤ ∞ 1\leq p\leq\infty , were introduced by Smith in [ 25 ] and Hassell et al. in [ 14 ] .

title: L p L^{p} theory for the square roots and square functions of elliptic operators having a BMO anti-symmetric part Thanks: S. Hofmann acknowledges support of the National Science Foundation (currently grant number DMS-1664047). S. Mayboroda is supported in part by the NSF grants DMS 1344235, DMS 1839
creator: Steve Hofmann, Linhan Li, Svitlana Mayboroda, Jill Pipher
description: Abstract . We consider the operator L = − div ( A ∇ ) L=-{\rm div}(A\nabla) , where A A is an n × n n\times n matrix of real coefficients and satisfies the ellipticity condition, with n ≥ 2 n\geq 2 .

title: Point Cloud Super Resolution with Adversarial Residual Graph Networks
creator: Huikai Wu Junge Zhang Kaiqi Huang
description: Abstract Point cloud super-resolution is a fundamental problem for 3D reconstruction and 3D data understanding. It takes a low-resolution (LR) point cloud as input and generates a high-resolution (HR) point cloud with rich details. In this paper, we present a data-driven method for point cloud super-resolution based on graph networks and adversarial losses.

title: Average preserving variation processes in view of optimization
creator: Rémi Lassalle
description: Abstract . In this paper, we investigate specific least action principles for laws of stochastic processes within a framework which stands on filtrations preserving variations. The associated Euler-Lagrange conditions, which we obtain, exhibit a deterministic process in the dynamics aside the canonical martingale term.

title: Acceleration of rank-constrained spatial covariance matrix estimation for blind speech extraction
creator: \authorblockN Yuki Kubo \authorrefmark 1, Norihiro Takamune \authorrefmark 1, Daichi Kitamura \authorrefmark 2, and Hiroshi Saruwatari \authorrefmark 1 \authorblockA \authorrefmark 1 The University of Tokyo, Graduate School of Information Science and Technology, Tokyo, Japan \authorblockA \authorref
description: Abstract In this paper, we propose new accelerated update rules for rank-constrained spatial covariance model estimation, which efficiently extracts a directional target source in diffuse background noise. The naive update rule requires heavy computation such as matrix inversion or matrix multiplication.

title: Functional probabilistic programming for scalable Bayesian modelling
creator: Jonathan Law, Darren J. Wilkinson
description: Abstract Bayesian inference involves the specification of a statistical model by a statistician or practitioner, with careful thought about what each parameter represents. This results in particularly interpretable models which can be used to explain relationships present in the observed data.

title: Selfsimilar Hessian manifolds
creator: Pavel Osipov
description: Abstract A selfsimiar manifold is a Riemannian manifold ( M , g ) \left(M,g\right) endowed with a homothetic vector field ξ \xi . We characterize global selfsimilar manifolds and describe the structure of local selfsimilar manifolds. We prove that any selfsimilar manifold with a potential homothetic vector field is a conical Riemannian manifold or a Eucledean space.

title: EdgeNet: A novel approach for Arabic numeral classification
creator: S.M.A. Sharif, Ghulam Mujtaba, S. M. Nadim Uddin
description: Abstract Despite the importance of handwritten numeral classification, a robust and effective method for a widely used language like Arabic is still due. This study focuses to overcome two major limitations of existing works: data diversity and effective learning method. Hence, the existing Arabic numeral datasets have been merged into a single dataset and augmented to introduce data diversity.

title: On the Existence of Simpler Machine Learning Models
creator: Lesia Semenova, Cynthia Rudin, Ronald Parr
description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Lesia Semenova, Cynthia Rudin, Ronald Parr. It is almost always easier to find an accurate-but-complex model than an accurate-yet-simple model. Finding optimal, sparse, accurate models of various forms (linear models with integer coefficients, decision sets, rule lists, decision trees) is generally NP-hard. We often do not know whether the search for a simpler model will be worthwhile, and thus we do not go to the trouble of searching for one.

title: Total graph of a signed graph Journal: Journal
creator: Francesco Belardo, Zoran Stanić, Thomas Zaslavsky
description: Abstract The total graph is built by joining the graph to its line graph by means of the incidences. We introduce a similar construction for signed graphs. Under two similar definitions of the line signed graph, we define the corresponding total signed graph and we show that it is stable under switching.

title: Generalized Lens Categories via Functors 𝒞 op → 𝖢𝖺𝗍 \mathcal{C}^{\mathrm{op}}\to{\mathsf{Cat}}
creator: David I. Spivak
description: Abstract Lenses have a rich history and have recently received a great deal of attention from applied category theorists. We generalize the notion of lens by defining a category 𝖫𝖾𝗇𝗌 F {\mathsf{Lens}}_{F} for any category 𝒞 \mathcal{C} and functor F : 𝒞 op → 𝖢𝖺𝗍 F\colon\mathcal{C}^{\mathrm{op}}\to{\mathsf{Cat}} , i.e. an indexed category, using a variant of the Grothendieck construction.
